28e1d1260afbf651: An owner's representative is a professional who acts only for the person paying for a building project. On a villa, we set the budget and programme, help appoint the consultant and contractor, control cost and time, report progress, handle variations and claims, and lead handover.
5e0b3ae70ed7ad98: Do I need an owner's representative to build a villa in Dubai?
084fd2d9115498e8: It isn't required by law. It is most valuable on bespoke villas, major renovations, and projects where the owner is often abroad or has not built before. We will tell you honestly if you don't need us.
771647015e830a41: How is that different from the consultant I have to appoint?
43e5eb40da6a1e49: In Dubai, a registered consultant carries the statutory design, submission and supervision responsibilities. They owe you proper professional care in that role. We add independent coordination and commercial scrutiny alongside them, acting only for you on cost, time, decisions, contracts and quality.
87214ecae0d9d9fa: Our founder, Philip Chapman, leads every Eastbridge appointment personally and is the person you speak to from the first conversation to handover. He is supported by a team of three project managers who attend site and provide cover when he is unavailable.
fd160f1c73f80327: Who attends site, and who covers when Philip is away?
0a6759b39e4bf52d: Philip leads every appointment and attends site himself. He is supported by a team of three project managers who attend site and provide cover when he is unavailable, for example when he is travelling. How often we attend site is agreed in writing in your appointment.
76ce0a9357ba196c: How often will you be on site?
c875e5b5f5e6440c: It is agreed in writing in the scope of your appointment, before work starts. Attendance follows the stage of the project: typically weekly during active construction and more often at key stages. See how an appointment works in the UAE.
a8f29f5f78e620f9: Who appoints the quantity surveyor, engineers and other specialists?
2751d654ccfcc4b5: You do, and you pay them directly. We help you work out what is needed, compare proposals like-for-like and choose. We take no commission or referral fee from anyone we help you appoint.
265baa0eb87e8dd4: Do you handle permits, supervision or legal advice?
7b278bef2ee4c419: No. Statutory design, authority submissions and supervision are the duties of the registered consultant you appoint, and legal advice should come from a UAE-qualified lawyer. Our role is commercial and project management on your side, alongside them.
f427917ad026dedd: Do you take commission from contractors?
e30aeec41b74ed6f: Never. We are paid only by you. See our independence pledge.

e4a9b7c848cf6e19: A bank guarantee the contractor provides in return for an up-front payment from the owner, usually at mobilisation. If the contractor fails to perform before the advance has been earned back, the owner can call on the guarantee. The advance is normally recovered by deducting an agreed share from each interim payment, and the guarantee should reduce as it is repaid. Check the wording, the issuing bank and the expiry date before releasing any money.

fdb433f68fce829c: In Abu Dhabi, a villa building permit is issued by the municipality through its services on TAMM, the emirate's government services platform, under regulations set by the Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT). Since June 2025, new private villa applications have been processed through Binaa, DMT's AI-assisted permits platform. In plot communities such as Saadiyat or Hudayriyat, you need the master developer's design approval first, and your registered consultant prepares and submits the application on your behalf.
3eb07ee82e1c5474: If you have built or renovated in Dubai, the shape will feel familiar, but the regulator, the platforms and the villa rules are different. This guide explains the Abu Dhabi route from the owner's side, and where it departs from Dubai.
c478172039ec6dea: Who issues villa building permits in Abu Dhabi?
a66195d7ff758803: The regulator. DMT sets planning and building regulations for the emirate, including the private villa regulations it amended in September 2025 (DMT).
caa22b4ca135782f: The municipality. The permit itself is issued by the municipality for the region where your plot sits: Abu Dhabi City, Al Ain or Al Dhafra. Your consultant will confirm which applies.
af26d366c76017eb: The platforms. TAMM is the front door for government services in Abu Dhabi, and lists the building permit, renewal and related construction services (TAMM). Behind it, Binaa handles the technical review of permit applications, and DMT's Unified Permitting System carries later construction-stage submissions.
f28491a04c04cffe: On top of that, if your plot sits in a master-planned community, the master developer has its own design guidelines and review. Aldar on Saadiyat and Modon on Hudayriyat are examples. Developer approval comes before the municipal application, not alongside it.
6276e64b15f50f59: Polgreen Manor, Mawgan Porth, Cornwall. Built by P Chapman Construction.
3a887557dea25a58: What is Binaa, and what does it change for villa owners?
279b2992e501da35: DMT launched Binaa in June 2025 as a digital permits platform using AI review tools, Building Information Modelling, and virtual and augmented reality (DMT). At launch, DMT said AI review of 2D plans would be introduced gradually, with those plans reviewed manually in the meantime. A few points are directly relevant to a private client:
d0c4edc07084c258: Villas went first. Phase one of the rollout covered new private villas, which DMT said account for around 20,000 applications a year.
d1c8f1eb38e2e237: It looks for over-design. DMT says the platform is intended to flag designs that use unnecessarily complex methods or heavy materials for small villas. That is a cost question as much as a compliance one.
4dd87e5dfa03c9e9: Reviews are coordinated. Binaa was launched under an agreement with Abu Dhabi Civil Defence Authority, TAQA and e&, so that data, documents and technical reviews are shared rather than chased one by one.
42f78f059ef1b1ce: Owners can see progress. DMT says owners, consultants and contractors can monitor an application's progress on the platform.
9f82537d4f020255: The early results are reported by the government itself. In March 2026 the Abu Dhabi Media Office reported that the average time to issue a residential villa building permit had fallen by 57% since Binaa launched, that resubmissions had dropped by 53%, and that DMT issued more than 11,000 building permits in 2025 (Abu Dhabi Media Office).
d12e498f26ceeff3: What are the steps to get a villa permit in Abu Dhabi?
2c6d89952757009c: The sequence below is how we would plan it from the owner's side. Your registered consultant will confirm the detail for your plot and municipality.
e35fc1a6822daf8d: Confirm what the plot allows. Site plan, the master developer's design guidelines if any, and the current DMT villa regulations.
de0911fc86f847cb: Appoint a registered consultant. In Abu Dhabi, engineering consultants and contractors are licensed and classified through services on TAMM (TAMM). Check registration before you sign.
e8f5d9db9a7e3354: Design to the brief and the rules. Concept, then detailed design, including the Estidama Pearl requirements (see below).
ba7f55f6e167a680: Master developer approval. Where it applies, submit to the developer and obtain its approval or no-objection.
bd3d08f2bfab47e6: Municipal permit application. Your consultant submits the drawings and documents. TAMM's listing for a new building permit names approved plans and architectural layout drawings among the documents, and shows a 10 working day service time at the time of writing (TAMM).
5cdebd9b2fc01410: Start on site within the permit's life. TAMM's renewal service says a permit can be renewed once, provided it has not exceeded its six-month validity (TAMM). Do not let a permit lapse while you are still choosing a contractor.
4563e76c2aeeab38: Construction-stage reporting and inspections. Your consultant and contractor report through the Unified Permitting System, and the authority inspects.
abb2c4024aa49913: Completion and connection. Final inspections, completion documentation and utility connections before you move in.
c16e2d143c64dad0: Circular No. 9 of 2026, issued by DMT's Urban Planning and Permits Centre, replaces traditional phase-closure permits with certified technical reports for designated categories of project. The registered consultant responsible for supervising the works and the contractor prepare a dated, signed report with photographs covering the works, inspections and corrective actions, and the two share legal liability for non-compliance. The centre continues unannounced site visits. The circular does not waive mandatory field inspections where physical verification is required, or clearances from other bodies such as Abu Dhabi Civil Defence (WAM, Khaleej Times).
ff1a1a40179f51ea: For an owner, this is a meaningful shift. More of the assurance that work matches the approved drawings now rests on reports written by the people doing and supervising the work. That makes it more important, not less, that the owner has an independent view of what is actually happening on site.

Two differences catch owners out most often. First, a consultant who knows Dubai's process well is not automatically the right choice in Abu Dhabi; ask specifically about recent Abu Dhabi villa submissions and Estidama. Second, the villa regulations themselves differ, so a design brief written with a Dubai villa in mind may need rethinking before a single line is drawn.
e96f37c286abbd1b: What do Abu Dhabi's private villa regulations allow?
a996e0b30046db6a: DMT's September 2025 amendments loosened several rules that shape a villa's design (DMT):
3d986bbe0f03cf14: A closed, lightweight rooftop majlis can be added without affecting the land-use percentage.
faf789448421d3c1: The front setback from the street is reduced to 1.5 metres.
1d476fab8c7b9748: Guest annexes may have a first floor or a basement, provided they are not built against the boundary wall.
007063c248888fb9: Shading structures do not count towards the building footprint.
7975dab07a80ea52: The whole flat roof can be built on, provided a 1.5 metre setback is kept.
867d08847f20b7fa: Two villas can sit next to each other without a separating wall, with the owners' agreement.
6a39787f67fbe39c: This follows earlier changes in 2019, when Abu Dhabi reduced minimum sizes for bedrooms, kitchens, dining rooms and majlis areas, removed the requirement for an internal hallway, and cut the maximum side fence height from six metres to four (Gulf News). The direction of travel is towards flexibility, but master developer guidelines can still be stricter than the emirate's rules. Read both.
60811ec9594aae46: What is the Estidama Pearl rating, and does a villa need it?
c124fd5843898e07: Estidama is Abu Dhabi's sustainability programme, and the Pearl Rating System is its building rating tool. New villas must achieve at least a 1 Pearl rating, which means meeting all the mandatory credits, documented through the approvals process (DMT). Higher ratings need additional credit points. In our experience, requirements of this kind are cheapest when they shape the design from the start, and expensive when they arrive as a late compliance exercise.
88a5fae2df9e5bfa: Do I need a permit for a pool, extension or renovation?
a30264790f5ab254: Usually yes, but the route is lighter than a new build. Since August 2025, DMT has let contractors obtain permits directly for defined minor works on villas, farmhouses and holiday homes, including concrete and metal structures, extensions of up to 25 square metres, non-structural modifications, maintenance and interior finishing, swimming pools, canopies, shade structures and fences (DMT).
c7b6d341c0d9ea73: That is convenient, and it also changes who holds the paperwork. If your contractor obtains the permit, make sure the scope in the permit matches the scope you are paying for, and that you receive copies. In a master community, check the developer's own requirements as well.
b8df95764b0e5a0d: Can a foreign owner build a villa in Abu Dhabi?
00ce6060c347d917: Foreign nationals can own property in designated investment zones in Abu Dhabi (UAE Government portal). Confirm the ownership position for your specific plot with a UAE-qualified lawyer before you buy; this guide is not legal advice.
0743576c33e6d460: A view from the builder's side
4ef6b74c6985a9c0: For 21 years we were the contractor waiting on approvals, and we learned to read the start date from the state of the drawings, not the date of the application. The trouble usually began earlier: Drawings submitted before the owner had really decided the brief, then revised after comments. A contractor appointed on permit drawings that were never detailed enough to price properly. A start date that slipped because nobody had booked the team while the application was in.
1249c9433345b7a6: On our side of the table, a fast permit was only good news if the drawings behind it were complete. When they were not, we priced the gaps as risk, and later as variations. Abu Dhabi's faster digital review is genuinely helpful. It does not remove the need for the owner to settle the brief, check the design against the budget, and have the contractor selection running in parallel, so that a permit with a limited life turns into a start on site.

e4eb3a642bf45a01: Settle the brief and budget before detailed design begins, and freeze major decisions before submission.
a1ee04fc84e0cb90: Check your consultant's recent Abu Dhabi villa experience, including Estidama and the specific master developer.

36d127bef88a0479: Run contractor selection in parallel with the approvals, so the permit does not lapse waiting for a start.
965c6a16b3f1b1b7: Keep copies of every approval, drawing revision and permit in your own records, not only your team's.
8fdb01f80e916d74: Have someone independent of the contractor and the consultant reading the construction-stage reports.

4c65348013cadd04: Who issues building permits for villas in Abu Dhabi?
b6c6fd8713dc62eb: Permits are issued by the municipality, through its services on the TAMM platform, under regulations set by the Department of Municipalities and Transport. In master-planned plot communities, the master developer's design approval normally comes first.
20c2de4832958bd8: What is Binaa in Abu Dhabi?
c9c3c958c7f2c83b: Binaa is DMT's digital building permits platform, launched in June 2025. It uses AI review tools and BIM to check designs, coordinates reviews with Civil Defence, TAQA and e&, and started with new private villas as its first phase.
87ad7152f30dac0c: How long does a villa building permit take in Abu Dhabi?
10cba42891860103: TAMM's service listing for a new building permit shows a 10 working day service time, and DMT reports a 57% reduction in average villa permit times since Binaa launched. Allow longer overall for design development, master developer review and resubmissions.
d2eb982dc46db215: Do I need a permit for a pool or small extension in Abu Dhabi?
9f84a38059ec6526: Yes, but since August 2025 contractors can obtain permits directly for defined minor works, including extensions up to 25 square metres, pools, canopies, shade structures and fences, without the full new-build route.
3c4f29acf0cab3a8: Is the Abu Dhabi villa permit process the same as Dubai's?
cdec4b907bb47d22: No. The regulator, the platforms, the villa regulations and the sustainability requirements are all different. Owners who have built in Dubai should not assume their experience transfers directly.

4a1f767a94e35932: Most of a Dubai villa build can be run from the UK, but a handful of decisions (plot, design freeze, finishes, handover) are far better made in person.
a6842db4be4604ef: Insist on three things every week or month: a dated photo report, an updated cost-to-complete, and a decision log showing what you approved and when.
d700c8a364461da2: Never release a payment you cannot tie to an agreed milestone and a valuation from the consultant, however urgent the request sounds.
48a9cbb4f45bc60d: UAE villa contracts and site roles differ from UK JCT practice; the registered consultant usually holds the contract administration role, not an architect you appoint as in the UK.
6a27f8cb1420d475: Absentee projects rarely fail through one big event; they fail through small, unrecorded changes that nobody challenged at the time.

b932d04ec515b155: Yes, you can build a villa in Dubai while living in the UK, and many owners do. Design development, approvals, payments and most progress monitoring can be handled remotely if the reporting is disciplined. What cannot be delegated without risk are a small number of decisions about the plot, the design freeze, finishes and handover, and the habit of checking every payment against something you can verify.
8ed3f9f864e23f9f: This article sets out what works from a distance, what needs you in the room, and where we see absentee projects drift.
fa7a21a075231d9e: What can you do remotely on a Dubai villa build?
65d697f4f5c8f49e: More than most people expect. Dubai's permit process is now largely digital: the authorities run a single window for building permits that links Dubai Municipality, the Dubai Development Authority, Trakhees and the service providers (Dubai Municipality). Your registered consultant makes those submissions; you do not need to be in Dubai for them to happen.
1083aa2efe22475e: From the UK you can realistically:
d39a59d577af036a: Review and comment on concept and developed designs over video calls and shared drawings.
a0508a625ab4ea7d: Approve the brief, the budget and the programme.
48a5116fbcfe5fd8: Compare contractor bids, with help, and decide who to appoint.
f45e22db904ab2a5: Approve or reject variations, provided you have a clear process for doing so.
9f17004c9df33c54: Release stage payments against agreed milestones.
3a351f0853ea9408: Follow progress through photographs, video walkrounds and written reports.
7ae481f7fb53870b: The design and approvals phase is the easiest part to run remotely. Published guidance puts design at around three to four months and approvals at two to three months, with construction typically eight to fourteen months on top (Real Estate Club Dubai). During those first six months or so, most of the work is on paper. We break the timeline down in how long it takes to build a villa in Dubai.
22a6eed4cf668eff: Blue Seas, Constantine Bay, Cornwall. Built by P Chapman Construction.
9ff7e7e1dbd92735: Which decisions need you there in person?
ff635b37c7a336b3: In our experience, four moments justify a flight.
25648ef3935243da: Orientation, views, neighbours, access and noise do not show up on an affection plan. See our plot checks.
8a21e2d07d4d7e17: Walking the plot with the drawings in hand catches level, view and privacy problems while they are still cheap to fix.
d44324c8a47f07ed: Stone, timber, joinery samples and lighting look different under Dubai sun than on a screen. Approve physical samples and keep them on site as the reference.
030520de6a602573: Snagging is a physical exercise. You need to open, run, flush and test things. Our snagging checklist covers what to look at.
4928027f4a3f3485: A mid-construction visit, when the structure is complete and first-fix services are in, is also worth making. It is the last point at which you can see what is going into the walls and ceilings before it disappears.
432f4b8b74028ad3: What reporting should you insist on?
9baaba59a21e302b: On the contractor's side, we learned that the clients who asked for structured information got a better-run job, because the discipline of producing it forced us to look at our own numbers. Ask for the following from the start, and write it into appointments where you can.
36d608cef2986e5e: Dated, labelled photographs organised by area, not a stream of images on a messaging app. Each set should show the same locations week on week so progress (or lack of it) is obvious. Include close-ups of anything about to be covered: waterproofing, insulation, pipework, cable routes, structural connections.
c45c03fad2b80abd: Not just what has been paid, but what it will cost to finish. A sound cost report shows the original contract sum, approved variations, pending variations, provisional sums spent and remaining, contingency used, and a forecast final cost. If the forecast only changes when someone asks, it is not a forecast.
683017dd4661595c: The current programme against the baseline, with the critical path marked and any slippage explained. Look for activities whose dates quietly move each month.
b5644513cb21af9d: A single running record of every decision you have made: what was asked, what you approved, the date, and any cost or time effect. When disputes arise months later, the decision log is usually the most useful document on the project. It also protects you from the phrase "the client asked for it" being applied to things you never approved.
18f263df4c1764fc: Our site visits and reporting and cost and programme control services are built around exactly these documents.
e02d43b37a0408cb: How do payments and banking work from the UK?
50d712a2b01f5bc0: Keep this simple and auditable. Practical points, in general terms:
1e5debed9172926a: Pay against milestones, not requests. Stage payments should follow a schedule in the contract and a valuation of work done from the consultant. Treat any request for money "to secure materials" or "to keep the crew on site" outside that schedule as a conversation, not a payment.
3ad8d56d24e29ad9: Use a UAE account where sensible. Many owners open a local account to make payments to contractors and authorities more straightforward. Banks' requirements for non-residents vary, so ask them directly.
cb45b41fdda23a16: Watch currency exposure. The dirham is pegged to the US dollar, so a build funded from sterling carries sterling-to-dollar exchange risk over a programme that may run well over a year. Some owners convert in tranches against the payment schedule. Speak to your bank or a currency specialist.
4e33ce8178a57e0d: Keep a payment register. Every payment, its reference to a milestone or approved variation, and the supporting valuation. Reconcile it against the cost report monthly.
25adb6761a072176: Know what you are holding back. Retention and advance payment arrangements should be clear in the contract and tracked, because they are your main leverage at the end of the job.
c1bb3e41b6af8bdf: None of this is financial or tax advice. If the build has UK tax implications for you, speak to your own advisers.
d4a49cfef023913a: Time zones: the hidden programme risk
9e6e4fcc9166344e: The UAE is four hours ahead of the UK in winter and three hours ahead during British Summer Time, and does not change its clocks. That sounds manageable, but it has a real effect. Site teams often start early in the day to avoid the heat, so by the time a UK owner is at their desk, the site has been working for hours. A question raised on site at 8am Dubai time may not get your answer until their afternoon, and a decision needed on a Friday may wait until the following week.
79855a6191577879: A fixed weekly call at a time that suits both sides, with a written agenda and minutes.
074fd7931cdef469: A defined turnaround for owner decisions, for example 48 hours, agreed with the contractor and consultant.
ffbcbc3c9b7f4ea3: Someone on the ground with clear, limited authority to deal with small site queries so they do not stall work.
bd533690f54311e6: Do you need a power of attorney?
00e09a474473eb8f: Sometimes. A power of attorney can make life easier for authority submissions, utility connections, handover formalities and signing documents when you cannot travel. It can also be dangerous if it is drawn too widely. A general power of attorney over your property affairs is a very different instrument from one limited to specific tasks on a specific project.
cc9fa95ef1554145: A power of attorney signed in the UK typically needs to go through notarisation and attestation steps before it can be used in the UAE. The detail changes and depends on the purpose, so take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on scope, form and process before you sign anything.
6c8a87c2ce0f770b: How does UAE construction practice differ from the UK?
1ff799e24ce215fb: Owners who have built in the UK often assume the same rules apply. The principles are familiar, but several things are different.
ee8ba5098602c112: In the UK, most private residential work uses JCT forms, with an architect or contract administrator issuing instructions and certificates under the contract. In Dubai, the Municipality publishes standard forms for engineering consultancy and construction contracting for private villas (Dubai Municipality), and many projects use FIDIC-style terms. Read our guide to villa construction contracts in the UAE for more, and have any contract reviewed by a UAE-qualified lawyer.
6ae5e1fd623cd2d7: In Dubai, the registered consultant typically designs the villa, makes the authority submissions and carries the formal site role through construction, including assessing the contractor's payment applications. That is a regulated role. The owner appoints the consultant and the contractor separately, and the consultant's position sits between the two. An owner's representative such as Eastbridge is a different role: we act only for the owner, alongside the consultant and the contractor, and do not replace either. Our article on owner's representative vs project manager vs consultant explains the difference.
51864663f6de00d8: UAE law imposes a ten-year liability on the main contractor and the engineer for serious structural defects, now set out in Articles 821 to 824 of the new Civil Code in force from 1 June 2026; it cannot be contracted out of (Charles Russell Speechlys). There is no direct UK equivalent for a one-off private house, though the protection is narrower than many owners assume. Take legal advice on how it applies to you.
9c071125f4af66c4: UK residential contractors are used to clients who visit regularly and argue every variation. In Dubai, the volume of work and the spread of contractor capability are both wide. Some firms run well-documented, transparent jobs. Others rely on the owner not being there. Your reporting regime tells the contractor which kind of client you are.
b4d922aef7817dae: Common failure modes for absentee owners
97496a27e16b4129: Every builder sees these from the other side of the table. They are not unique to Dubai, but distance makes each one worse.
d4fc04337725d5c6: Verbal approvals. A quick "yes, fine" on a call becomes a variation nobody priced. Every approval should go into the decision log, in writing, with its cost.
bde9b4983535a018: Payments ahead of progress. Once the contractor has been paid for work not yet done, your leverage has gone. This is the single most common way absentee builds get into trouble.
70e2ee5df93d2e32: Design that was never truly frozen. Small changes during construction cost far more than the same changes on paper, and each one gives the contractor a legitimate reason to ask for more time.
0787fa3d0dbc075c: Provisional sums left vague. On the contractor's side, the first thing we looked at on any job was where the provisional sums sat and how loosely they were described. That is where final accounts grow.
8a0161c03308a21f: Nobody independent looking. Photographs chosen by the contractor show what the contractor wants you to see. An independent visit, unannounced where possible, sees what is actually there.
baf4803a6e27db0d: Late finishes decisions. If you have not chosen tiles, sanitaryware or joinery when the programme needs them, the delay is yours, and so is the cost.
abe0baa9839cf2d6: Handover from a distance. Accepting the keys without a proper snagging inspection usually means a long defects period of chasing by email.
b1e4b76f3f3af5e0: If a project has already drifted, our stalled project rescue work starts by rebuilding the cost, programme and decision record so you can see where you stand.
be02015eb2a15aba: We represent owners who are building in Dubai and Abu Dhabi but cannot be there every week. We work alongside your registered consultant and your contractor, carry out independent client-side site visits, and give you clear reporting on cost, programme and decisions so you can approve things with confidence from the UK. Our overseas owners page explains how we structure that. If you are planning a build or already part-way through one, get in touch.
54aa5273ab00b155: Can I build a villa in Dubai without living in the UAE?
b25bf2f29eb31aa8: Yes. Many owners run their build from abroad. You will need a registered consultant and a licensed contractor, a reliable way to receive reporting and approve decisions, and a plan for the few visits where being on site matters.
ea87fcf115cbc9a5: How often should I visit the site if I live in the UK?
f03a73a6b8c568a7: In our experience, aim to be present at the design freeze, the main finishes selections, a mid-construction walkround and the pre-handover inspection. Between those, good reporting and an independent representative on the ground can carry most of the load.
dc94ad59fc199c90: Do I need a power of attorney to build in Dubai?
9566fab225ed55ab: Not always, but a carefully limited power of attorney can help with authority submissions, utility accounts and handover formalities. Its scope matters a great deal, so take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer before signing one.
52b2147cdd7a8ae4: Is a UAE construction contract similar to a JCT contract?
1833b130479b50c2: The principles are familiar, but the forms, roles and legal background differ. Dubai Municipality publishes standard forms for private villas, and many projects use FIDIC-style terms. Have any contract reviewed by a UAE-qualified lawyer.

bc6681593b6cf1a3: Why plot checks matter more than the price
8217643cf409cc3e: On the contractor's side, we priced many houses on plots the client had already bought, and the most expensive surprises were almost always baked in on the day they exchanged: a level change nobody had surveyed, a restrictive covenant, a drain running across the garden. The negotiation over a few percent on the land price mattered far less than these.
70d83b2256ebfc10: In Dubai the same logic applies, with the added layer of master developer rules. A plot is only worth what you are allowed, and can afford, to build on it.
1816c3604bec5d0e: Saqqara, Feock, Cornwall. Built by P Chapman Construction.
b56bc7027ff2b9ba: Ownership and title. Confirm the seller owns the plot and is entitled to sell it, and whether there is a mortgage or other restriction registered. Your lawyer will handle this through the proper channels.
d57cf3aae30578b6: Affection plan. The official plot plan sets out the plot number, area, boundaries, permitted use and other key details. Check the area matches what you are paying for, and that the permitted use is residential villa.
8984a66eb9ddf3d5: Payment status. If the plot was bought off a master developer on a payment plan, confirm what has been paid, what remains, and what the developer requires to transfer.
49234214128c98ba: Master developer consent. Transfers in master communities usually need a no-objection letter from the master developer, which may depend on service charges being up to date.
3e8171cb6ce18c4b: Every master community has rules on what you can build. They sit on top of the authority's building regulations, and they are where a plot's real capacity is decided. Ask for the current design guidelines for the specific plot, not a brochure summary.
0e1feea3da2cd44f: Minimum distances from front, side and rear boundaries, and from the waterfront where relevant
ac600dbdda0f8501: Maximum height, number of floors, roof structures, basements
3ea132968c698190: Maximum footprint as a share of the plot, and total built-up area allowed
a4c3b7c85f6e3526: Required materials, colours, roof forms, façade treatments
8b172b5da1068764: Wall heights, materials, transparency to the street or water
c0bbd8054ecc41e6: Pools, pavilions, majlis, staff quarters, jetties
e32d309a8efec9ad: Dates by which design approval, construction start or completion must happen, and the consequences of missing them
42c3d48cd6b31183: Build-by deadlines deserve special attention. If you are buying a plot to hold rather than to build on straight away, an obligation to start construction within a set period can change your plans and your finances. Read the sale documents closely and take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer.
9df1435d27aef7d0: Remember too that authority rules can change. In Abu Dhabi, for example, the Department of Municipalities and Transport amended private villa regulations in September 2025, including changes to rooftop majlis, a 1.5 m front setback and annex basements (DMT). Your registered consultant should confirm the current rules for your plot, in Dubai or Abu Dhabi.
2a2ae91bf7621e27: Which authority will approve your villa?
acad16f0e84f213e: In Dubai, permits come through a single unified window that links Dubai Municipality, the Dubai Development Authority, Trakhees and the utility and service providers (Dubai Municipality). Which authority applies depends on where your plot sits. Your consultant will confirm this; in master communities you will typically also need the master developer's approval or no-objection before the authority permit. Our design and approvals page explains how we support that process.
fe74b29d1b6ffe4c: Plots in master communities usually carry service charges from the day you own them, whether or not you have built. Check:
a720c82b9e2d4b9e: The current annual charge and how it is calculated.
d0c5fa2a2a25ee1a: Whether charges are up to date (arrears can delay transfer).
6a0757de80cb3112: Any planned increases or special levies for infrastructure.
945cd70dd16b09eb: How charges change once the villa is complete.
8fd4a86a50f02b88: Much of Dubai's prime villa land is reclaimed or coastal, and ground conditions vary. Before committing:
d3cca37abc49c3a3: Ask whether a geotechnical investigation exists for the plot or nearby plots, and read it.
ac4d36644559e724: Understand the likely foundation type. Piled foundations cost significantly more than shallow ones.
e483a6557afc996e: If you want a basement, ask about groundwater level. Dewatering during construction and long-term waterproofing of a basement below the water table add cost and risk.
e873e5c12d9d7f1c: Check for any fill or contamination issues the seller or developer is aware of.
c8e4edfd369da760: In our experience, foundations and below-ground work are where early budgets move most, because they are priced before anyone has dug a hole.
cea61b743c898bfb: Are water, power, sewerage and telecoms available at the plot boundary now, or are they promised?
482f72c3d5b35fa6: Who pays for the connections, and are there capacity limits?
7c7e5e4dd8bc2fd4: Is the road access complete and adopted?
326dea53346d515b: For newer communities, what is the delivery schedule for infrastructure, and what happens if it slips?
7ffdbcf8e5096764: Published guidance puts permits, NOCs and utility connections at roughly AED 25,000 to 75,000, or 2 to 5% of build cost (Real Estate Club Dubai). Treat that as a guide, not a quote.
91c98f3c795401a1: Stand on the plot and look around. Then check what the guidelines allow your neighbours to build. A vacant plot next door today may become a three-storey villa that overlooks your pool. Ask:
1f3098776e457068: What is the maximum height and setback on adjoining plots?
dff700fe07594904: Are any neighbours already building, and in what state is their site?
62011cdc2aeb381f: Will a neighbour's construction affect your access, noise or programme?
096e50d70873ffa4: Is there anything planned nearby, such as a road, a utility building or a commercial plot?
a84242c9af56ecfe: Realistic build budget against plot price
9417557dfe560a93: This is where many plot purchases go wrong. Owners spend months negotiating the land and then discover the villa they want costs far more than expected.
6dc70e543057c12b: Published construction-only ranges for Dubai villas, 2025 to 2026, from Engel & Völkers:
28a67a37685f1ace: On top of construction, add design and engineering (Engel & Völkers quotes AED 50,000 to 150,000 for design, engineering and permits), a contingency (10 to 15% is commonly quoted), pool, landscaping and furniture. At the top end, furniture, fittings and equipment alone are quoted at 30 to 40% on top (Real Estate Club Dubai).
9cd743d3c4078dc0: Take the maximum built-up area the guidelines allow, or the area you actually want.
e3a258e3e1775a62: Apply a construction rate matched to the specification you expect.
69949001b62780fb: Add design, approvals, contingency, pool, landscaping and furniture.
448c9c90a56adeac: Add finance and holding costs, including service charges, for the duration of the build.
2c5664773394f443: On a prime plot, the villa can easily cost as much as, or more than, the land. Our guide to villa construction cost in Dubai goes into more detail.
5295f3758989d56b: Ask the hard question early: what would this finished villa sell for? Compare plot price plus total build cost against recent sales of comparable completed villas in the same community. If the combined cost is close to or above that figure, you are building for lifestyle rather than investment, which is a legitimate choice, but it should be a conscious one. Use an independent valuer for this.
97e0385e2a302053: New plot markets: Hudayriyat, Dubai Islands and Palm Jebel Ali
7a7c4567ae682683: Several newer communities are now selling plots for private villas.
f8c68b36cc4de6c4: Hudayriyat, Abu Dhabi. Modon launched its first residential plots community on Hudayriyat Island, with more than 1,700 plots for four to six bedroom villas (Middle East Construction News). Abu Dhabi's approvals run through a different system from Dubai's, under the Department of Municipalities and Transport. See our Hudayriyat page.
7af164bed8fea53c: If you are buying in Abu Dhabi, our guide to villa permits in Abu Dhabi explains how approvals there differ from Dubai.
3f1f4dcb6e9fc1d1: Dubai Islands and Palm Jebel Ali. Both are Nakheel master communities where plots are being sold for private villas. As newer markets, they have fewer completed villas to benchmark against, so evidence on actual build costs, timelines and resale values is thinner. That can be an opportunity, but it raises the importance of checking infrastructure delivery dates, the precise design guidelines, any build-by obligations and the master developer's approval process. 53b521caeeae6e42: A Dubai villa permit is applied for online by your registered engineering consultant, through Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority depending on where your plot sits, using the unified building permit window.
84fcd591faf1065e: In a master-planned community the master developer's NOC normally comes first; service-authority NOCs such as DEWA and Civil Defence are then gathered through the unified window.
74fd7772d8ad06e9: The owner does not submit drawings, but signs the consultant's appointment, provides title and plot documents, approves the design and pays the fees.
ec52fb41310750c6: A clean permit submission can be decided quickly, but market guides put the whole approvals stage at 2–3 months because of comment rounds, NOCs and late design changes.
bdc1a9547c244157: Most permit delay is caused by information, not by the authority: incomplete drawings, design changes after submission and a contractor appointed too late to register.
ce360c34c86bcf99: Who issues villa building permits in Dubai?
87e1a3dd39933ed7: How long does a Dubai villa permit take?
71891a5d95396afa: How long is a building permit valid?
d1b69eaf688e9dd8: Can work start before the building permit?
e5988b868ba7749c: How do you keep the permit stage on track?
c8b1a8d10b40e996: A villa building permit in Dubai is applied for online by your registered engineering consultant, not by you. The consultant submits the drawings and fees through the unified building permit window to Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits; service-authority NOCs are gathered through the same system; and the permit is issued with stamped drawings. The owner's part is to appoint the team, provide the plot documents, approve a design that is genuinely finished, and pay the fees on time.
216fbd50d4e2b691: Who issues villa building permits in Dubai?
2524510782d24e13: Three authorities issue building permits for private villas in Dubai: Dubai Municipality, Trakhees and the Dubai Development Authority. Which one applies depends on where your plot sits, and your consultant will confirm it at the start.
244a472d4879d8a0: Since 2022, building permits across Dubai Municipality, the Dubai Development Authority, Trakhees and DIEZ have run through a single unified e-window, with Civil Defence, RTA, DEWA, Etisalat and du linked in (Dubai Municipality). In October 2023 Dubai Municipality launched the Build in Dubai platform, which covers the whole life of a project: land, design, permits, construction, completion, connection and later alterations (Dubai Media Office). The Dubai Building Permits app was relaunched in August 2024 with a registry and ratings for consultants and contractors.
095ca8d195ea09a0: Designs are checked against the Dubai Building Code, whose 2021 edition has a dedicated part for villas (Part K). In practice that means the code, not a reviewing engineer's preference, is the yardstick your drawings are measured against.
3ed54f49c8379771: The sequence below follows Dubai Municipality's published procedure for residential buildings, with the master-developer step that applies in most private villa communities. Other authorities follow a similar logic with their own portals.
04dfae3b5a6a3a72: Affection plan, master-developer guidelines and site constraints reviewed; consultant appointed
a9bcb40b040e04ac: Signs consultancy agreement, provides title and plot documents
84bf83d2be5a8c9d: Layout, massing and areas fixed; optional initial design concept approval
1bde0db7f788b36e: Signs developer forms, pays developer fees
f184b7ae8b0ebef2: Architectural, structural, MEP, insulation, drainage and civil defence drawings
ac296d7bfa9848bf: Answers design questions, freezes the layout
761eae18b69dd76d: Drawings, building card details and fees submitted online
75e57dd3ba1ae0cf: DEWA, Civil Defence, telecoms and others review through the unified window
0774505d1923483f: Usually nothing, unless a design change is needed
f1fcaefb48ec7f33: Permit and stamped drawings issued, printable online
4dd607df17526894: Checks the permit matches the design you approved
a78c5e608135ca56: Hoarding, excavation, shoring and piling, then the building itself
ef95adb894ef9925: Contractor, under the consultant's statutory role
91b039b02e20f7af: Shoring, foundations, slabs and similar stages inspected
67f5a9246e0091c2: Keeps decisions on time so inspections are not missed
6edb589d202a808a: Joint completion inspection, completion certificate, service connection
91b81ea57d8b5eee: Steps 5 to 10 follow Dubai Municipality's residential procedure. The document list in step 4 and the step 5 detail come from Dubizzle's guide to the new building permit; the site preparation permit in step 8 is described below.
d0a2e0232a02cdcf: What does the consultant actually submit?
4eb5e6c90292e82a: For a new villa, the submission covers architecture, structure, electromechanical systems, insulation and drainage, road layouts and civil defence, together with building card details and fees, through the Dubai Building Permits System (Dubizzle). Your consultant may also choose to seek an initial design concept approval before the final design; Dubizzle describes this as optional, a preliminary check of the architecture against codes and planning standards that does not allow work to start.
0857c9ffe95bb4d0: Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, engineering consultancy in Dubai, including in free zones, may only be practised by registered firms (Law No. 14 of 2025). That is why the submission sits with your consultant. It is also why the quality of the consultant you appoint has more effect on your permit timeline than anything the authority does.
2205efcadeb88fb4: The owner does not prepare drawings or make the technical submission, but the owner's signature and documents sit underneath all of it. In our experience, the owner's side typically covers:
3ba25bc69160e116: The consultant's appointment. Dubai Municipality publishes standard contract forms for consultancy and construction on private villas, in Arabic, which are a sensible baseline. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer before signing.
ef9a1125d3826b24: Proof of ownership and plot documents. Title deed, affection plan and any master-developer agreement or conditions attached to the plot.
b93a696119657117: Master-developer forms. In master communities the developer's NOC application normally needs the owner's authorisation and fees.
296939cf80a6dbbc: Design approval. A written sign-off of the drawings that will be submitted. This is the signature that matters most, because every change after it costs time.
e3641bd0e9f83122: Fees. Authority, developer and service-authority fees. Real Estate Club Dubai puts permits, NOCs and DEWA at AED 25,000–75,000, or 2–5% of the build cost.
8072d31147ed250d: The construction contract. Signed with the contractor you choose, ideally on a design that has already been permitted.
fa1bd81bdec17266: Your consultant will confirm the exact list for your authority and community. Ask for it in writing at appointment, with a date against each item.
4be328d303002686: How long does a Dubai villa permit take?
647fb23941bb6c6f: There are two honest answers. Dubizzle's guide says it typically takes around three working days to get a building permit once a complete application is in the system. Real Estate Club Dubai puts the whole approvals stage at 2–3 months.
c40574eead954d1d: The gap between those figures is the real story. Three working days describes a single clean decision. Two to three months describes what usually happens around it: master-developer review, service-authority NOCs, comments to answer, drawings to revise and resubmit, and owner decisions that arrive late. For how the permit fits into the whole build, see how long it takes to build a villa in Dubai.
94ef90eba646e344: Two recent changes point to faster decisions. In August 2026 Dubai Municipality announced an AI system to assess permit applications for private and investment villas against the Dubai Building Code, with a 26-week rollout in three stages: development and testing, a pilot with selected consultancy firms, then rollout to villa applications through Build in Dubai (Dubai Media Office). It was announced as a project to be implemented, not a service already live. Separately, since October 2025, Dubai Municipality has accredited engineering consultancies to issue self-build permits for Emirati citizens' villas without prior review by municipal engineers. Neither removes the need for a complete, coordinated design. An automated check is quicker to say no, too.
a3eb14d81a812a94: How long is a building permit valid?
3ccc587a58cefe77: Dubizzle's guide says a Dubai Municipality building permit is valid for six months from issue and can be renewed. Treat that as a reason to time the permit sensibly against contractor selection. A permit obtained long before you have a contractor ready can lapse, and a renewal is one more task on a programme that already has enough.
12ecbb9116d88606: Can work start before the building permit?
fced98620e9f139a: Early works run under their own permit. Dubai Municipality's site preparation permit covers hoarding, excavation, shoring and piling. It is applied for by the consultant through Build in Dubai, and the shoring and excavation application needs a soil test report, structural drawings and calculations for excavation, shoring and foundations, and third-party insurance. Dubizzle reports that it is valid for six months from issue.
77538077f1e686c7: On a programme-critical plot, especially one with a basement, using this route well can save weeks. It only works if the ground investigation was commissioned early, which is an owner's decision, not the consultant's.
a3493d8cc0e1a852: Where do villa permit programmes slip?
92a4f21835aa2527: From the builder's side, we saw the same pattern for two decades. The programme we were given assumed the permit would arrive on a date; the permit arrived later; and the reasons were almost never the authority's. Our founder, Philip Chapman, ran P Chapman Construction in the UK for 21 years. The regulators were different, but the causes of permit delay are much the same in any jurisdiction.
6eb341b890fec192: A design submitted before it was finished. When an owner is impatient, the temptation is to submit and resolve the detail later. Comments come back, the drawings change, and the resubmission takes longer than finishing the design would have. The fastest submissions we saw were the ones held back a fortnight to close out coordination.
ae57ff53a8d2d749: Changes after design sign-off. Moving a wall, adding a basement room or enlarging a terrace after submission can mean revised structural calculations, a new master-developer review and a fresh round of NOCs. What looks like a small change on the owner's side is a resubmission on the consultant's.
ae7756c6c23ce50d: An over-designed structure. In August 2025 Dubai Municipality warned villa engineering consultancies about over-designing structures and inflating construction costs (Gulf News). Over-design does not only cost money; it is often the reason a tender comes back over budget, the design is cut back, and the drawings go round again.
9bd8cdb2e86c6c90: The master developer treated as a formality. Developer guidelines on heights, setbacks, materials and colours are specific, and a design that ignores them is returned before the authority ever sees it.
a898a6dd83f2d670: Ground information arriving late. No soil report means no shoring design, and no shoring design means no site preparation permit. Commission the ground investigation as soon as the plot is secure.
dce9c42f79fcf0f2: The contractor appointed too late. The contractor needs to be registered and insured before works can start under the permit. A permit with no contractor ready is a permit ticking towards its expiry date.
601280ac71f6e7af: On the contractor's side, the first thing we checked on any new job was whether the permit drawings and the tender drawings were the same set. Surprisingly often they were not. Every difference between the two became a variation, and every variation became a conversation about time.
ad8d590b349f0737: How do you keep the permit stage on track?
a36067251f6eafae: Three habits make the most difference.
94b885165b63c363: Fix the brief before design starts. A written brief with rooms, areas, a basement decision and a budget is the cheapest document in the project to change. Our guide to what it costs to build a villa in Dubai helps set the budget honestly.
b8fbc70114637235: Ask for an approvals tracker. One page, updated weekly: what has been submitted, to whom, on what date, what comments are outstanding and who owes the next action. If your consultant cannot produce it, that tells you something.
47278436d9f2fc6b: Plan the contractor in parallel. Run contractor selection while the permit is in progress, on the permit drawings, so that the contract is signed shortly after the permit is issued. Our guide to choosing a villa contractor in Dubai covers what to compare, and how to build a villa in Dubai sets the permit within the full journey from plot to keys.
a37cbf972db285f2: If you are planning a renovation or extension rather than a new build, the same authorities apply, but the route starts with an alteration application; our guide to renovating a Palm Jumeirah villa shows how a Nakheel NOC fits ahead of the permit.
5674cacaca8d38ea: We represent the owner through design and approvals, alongside your DM-registered consultant, who prepares and submits the drawings. We help you write the brief, review the design against your budget before it is submitted, and keep an approvals tracker so you always know what is waiting and on whom. Our design and approvals management service explains how we work. To talk through your plot and programme, contact us.
ffdacbfd2da51de3: Who applies for a villa building permit in Dubai?
879522f7ac6480d5: Your appointed engineering consultant, registered in Dubai, submits the drawings and fees online through the relevant authority's system. Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, only registered consultancies may practise engineering consultancy in Dubai. The owner appoints the consultant, provides the plot documents, approves the design and pays the fees.
32c6fb861c13c94a: How long does a Dubai Municipality villa permit take?
f7d21f2703f885bc: One widely used property guide says a building permit typically takes around three working days once a complete application is in the system. Real Estate Club Dubai puts the whole approvals stage, including master-developer review, NOCs and comment rounds, at 2–3 months. The difference is mostly rework.
e4149d4583a8ae64: How long is a Dubai building permit valid?
38dcd6ce9ee73e1f: Dubizzle's guide to Dubai Municipality building permits says a permit is valid for six months from issue and can be renewed. Confirm the current rule for your authority with your consultant, because a permit that lapses before work starts creates avoidable delay.
5d33889b4e49dfc8: Can work start on site before the building permit is issued?
66a88de6c755fce5: Only under the right permit. Dubai Municipality operates a separate site preparation permit for hoarding, excavation, shoring and piling, applied for by the consultant, which needs a soil test report, structural drawings and third-party insurance. Starting any work without a permit risks fines and stop orders.
d064e0d882ad8c48: Do I need a Nakheel or Emaar NOC before the authority permit?
946dc20e1ea42f08: In master-planned communities, generally yes. The master developer reviews the design against its guidelines and issues its NOC before the authority permit. In Nakheel communities, for example, renovation and extension approvals begin with a Nakheel NOC application through its portal.

8b79eead0409383b: How can you shorten the time to build a villa?
b15913c9e9858701: A custom villa in Dubai typically takes 12–24 months from plot to keys, and 24–36 months for a custom luxury villa, according to Real Estate Club Dubai. Construction itself is usually 8–14 months; the rest goes on design, approvals, choosing a contractor and handover. On most projects the months that are lost are lost on paper, before and during the build, not in the concrete and blockwork.
1d5962a46f196d17: That last point is the one owners rarely hear. What follows is where the time actually goes, which steps you can shorten and which you cannot.
0eeead9c98a197ef: Here is the full journey, with published durations where they exist and our own planning allowances where they do not.
096c87e109d1ec2d: Sum of phases above, end to end
e231257e835d529e: The published 12–24 months is shorter than the phases added end to end because it assumes some of them overlap. Two things stand out. First, roughly a third to a half of the elapsed time passes before anyone breaks ground. Second, the phases are not fixed blocks. A well-run project overlaps some of them, for example by preparing the bid package while approvals are in progress. A poorly run one stretches each of them, usually because a decision is waiting on someone.
7f9d877251032de0: For the step-by-step sequence and who does what at each stage, see our guide on how to build a villa in Dubai.
4cccb998d9dd10b5: The Lookout, Mylor, Cornwall. Built by P Chapman Construction.
6f9705a83a65c1a5: Where do the months actually go?
fc4265d2cd806213: On paper, a villa programme looks like a construction programme with some design at the front. In reality, the critical path runs through information for most of the project.
653838eb87b67400: Design. Three to four months is realistic for a resolved design across architecture, structure and MEP. It is not realistic if the brief is still moving. Every change to room sizes, a basement or the façade sends the design back a step, and each step means redrawing, recoordinating and, later, repricing.
c1dc223f31248a4e: Approvals. The permit comes from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits, and the service-authority NOCs are now gathered through one online window. In a master-planned community, the master developer's own design review and NOC usually comes first, and that review can take longer than the permit.
0bf0fb905293827f: Bidding. Inviting bids, answering bidder questions, comparing returns like-for-like and negotiating the contract takes weeks, not days. Rushing it is a false economy, because the months you save here are often lost in variations and disputes later.
540fe667dae93227: Construction. This is where owners expect the time to go, and where it is easiest to see. It is also where earlier slippage surfaces, because late design information shows up as stoppages on site.
004b948aab1710c9: Handover. The building can be physically complete weeks before you can live in it. Dubai Municipality's residential procedure describes a joint completion inspection, the completion certificate and then service connection. Snagging runs in parallel.
82af31ca214b6136: From the contractor's side, we could usually tell within the first two months whether a job would finish on time. It was rarely the ground or the weather that told us. It was how quickly the client and the design team answered questions.
0485f9f91335b632: How long does a villa building permit take in Dubai?
6920f9e5e3a83038: Once the drawings are right, the permit itself is not usually the slow part. In August 2026 Dubai Municipality announced that it is developing an AI system to issue villa permits automatically, to be piloted and then rolled out in phases through Build in Dubai (Dubai Media Office); it is not yet the standard route. The months go on preparing a compliant submission, master-developer review and rounds of comments; our guide to the Dubai villa building permit sets out each step and where programmes slip. Abu Dhabi has moved the same way with its Binaa platform; see our Abu Dhabi villa permit guide.
40d0842e5050d262: How long does villa construction take, stage by stage?
43a4a0bf35a6674c: Published guidance puts construction at 8–14 months. The table below is our own rule of thumb for how that time is typically spread on a two-storey villa without a basement. Stages overlap, so the durations do not simply add up.
627bff70a005b65c: Ground conditions, water table, any basement
10c7b65257026d84: Number of floors, spans, authority inspections
881fe22402a6628e: MEP first fix and internal walls
307feceb0a3874e0: Add a basement and the substructure stage can easily double. Dubai Municipality's procedure refers to staged inspections, such as shoring, foundations and slabs, so each structural milestone also carries a short wait for inspection, which a good programme allows for.
64ed89d6b51182fb: Does the summer slow construction in Dubai?
78f7546a313c1eea: It changes the working day. The UAE midday break, run by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, bans outdoor work under direct sunlight from 12:30pm to 3pm every day between 15 June and 15 September. 2026 was its 22nd consecutive year. Exemptions include concrete pours and asphalt laying where the work cannot be interrupted (Khaleej Times).
8151c2fbb1006667: Contractors adapt with early starts, shaded work areas and by shifting internal trades into the hottest months. Even so, three months of shortened outdoor days, combined with heat and humidity, reduce output on structural and external work. In our view, a programme that shows the same weekly progress in August as in January has not been thought through. Ask the contractor how the summer is reflected in its programme, and which activities it plans to do then.
41dc6d26c8a1c893: What makes a villa build take longer?
8893f16468491550: In our experience, these are the usual culprits, roughly in order of how often we saw them:
cd3970b8ef8ab7c8: Late owner decisions. Tiles, sanitaryware, joinery and automation chosen after the programme needs them. The delay is the owner's, and so is the cost.
eb5f86930c96abf2: Design changes after the permit. Moving walls or adding floor area can mean resubmission and lost months.
5aa6c0e3a89e7d4c: Long-lead items ordered late. Large-format or structural glazing, imported stone, bespoke joinery, lifts and specialist cooling equipment can take months to arrive. If they are not ordered early, the programme waits for them.
db5a1ffd1b3c2562: Basements and difficult ground. Waterfront and reclaimed plots in particular can need shoring and dewatering that add weeks before the frame begins.
9d492bf7e6b90c2c: Slow answers to site questions. Each request for information from the contractor that waits a fortnight is a fortnight someone can claim.
545de41fd393f3c3: Contractor resources and cash flow. A contractor stretched across too many sites, or short of cash, slows down quietly. A valuation running ahead of physical progress is an early warning.
e36a4a49498e6d08: The end of the job. Commissioning, completion inspections, connections and snagging are often under-planned, and the last 5% of the work takes a disproportionate share of the time.
aaa7d07de436410c: On the contractor's side, we always planned the programme so that the client's decisions sat on the critical path. That is not sharp practice; it is how programmes are drawn. It does mean that any late owner decision becomes immediate, claimable delay. We explain how float works in what a builder knows that most villa owners don't.
42f2148a2c3993a3: Why does delay cost so much?
b8a14c5418000a04: Because many of the contractor's site costs are time-related. Turner & Townsend put contractor preliminaries in Dubai at 12–14% of the contract (as cited by PRASOON). Those costs are priced per week or per month, so every extra month on site carries its own cost before any additional work is done. Add the owner's own costs, such as rent elsewhere, finance and currency exposure, and a three-month overrun becomes a significant line in the budget. Our guide to what it costs to build a villa in Dubai sets out the full budget.
3315c492e81fbfb5: How can you shorten the time to build a villa?
f4326ce425687263: You cannot compress concrete curing or authority inspections. You can remove most of the waiting around them.
4fe9881403dc0772: Fix the brief before design starts. The cheapest month to change your mind is the first one.
5660e0459e2681ce: Finish the design before pricing. A complete design gives real bids, fewer provisional sums and fewer stoppages on site.
514c40b1632adb1f: Overlap where it is safe. Prepare the bid package while approvals run, rather than after.
fd6aaf410e77600c: Order long-lead items early. Identify them during design and agree when each must be ordered.
5faf29d95638c90d: Agree a decision schedule. List every owner decision with the latest date it can be made, and have the contractor confirm those dates against its programme.
4e455236f05eed0c: Test the programme at bid stage. An unusually short programme with low preliminaries is often a claim waiting to happen.
fd30fe258eb03382: Review progress monthly against the programme, not just the payments. Small slippage is easy to recover in month three and very hard in month eleven.
d38f6b5d8b1b8c0a: Plan the end early. Commissioning, inspections, connections and snagging should be on the programme from the start.
286293ffa9195ea1: If you are building from abroad, decision speed matters even more. Our guide to building a villa in Dubai from the UK covers how to keep approvals moving across time zones.
4ed7a2b2678c666c: We represent the owner, alongside your DM-registered consultant and your contractor. Our founder, Philip Chapman, ran P Chapman Construction for 21 years, so we read a contractor's programme the way a builder does: where the float sits, what is on the critical path and what will be claimed if it slips. 9198d9d04d0220d6: How long does it take to build a villa in Dubai from start to finish?
28485f94afa2282b: Real Estate Club Dubai puts the typical journey at 12–24 months from plot to keys: design 3–4 months, approvals 2–3 months, construction 8–14 months and snagging 1–2 months. A custom luxury villa typically takes 24–36 months.
26df0a2d0d9825de: Does the summer slow down villa construction in Dubai?
67eccca95447b6bd: It changes how sites work. The UAE midday break bans outdoor work under direct sunlight from 12:30pm to 3pm between 15 June and 15 September, with exemptions such as concrete pours that cannot be interrupted. Contractors adjust shift patterns, but a realistic programme allows for fewer productive outdoor hours in summer.
66f6cb5ce94010a9: How long does construction take once the contractor starts on site?
77275248ffa125b8: Published guidance puts construction at 8–14 months for a villa in Dubai. A large luxury villa with a basement, structural glazing and bespoke finishes will usually sit at or beyond the top of that range.
1135c8ce3e054262: What is the most common cause of delay on a private villa?
b515b384bf28be14: In our experience, information rather than labour or materials: drawings issued late, samples left unapproved, finishes chosen after the programme needs them, and design changes made after the permit or after work has started.

9773139e3119c46b: To build a villa in Dubai you check the plot, set a brief and budget, appoint a registered consultant to design it, secure master-developer and authority approvals, choose a contractor, build, then complete inspections, connect services and hand over. Real Estate Club Dubai puts the whole journey at 12–24 months from plot to keys, and 24–36 months for a custom luxury villa. The owner appoints every party and makes every key decision; the order in which those decisions are made decides most of the cost.
e3d2ff268dd5cf11: What are the stages of building a villa in Dubai?
cda73b008065a95b: The process is well defined. Dubai Municipality's "Building in Dubai" platform, launched in October 2023, covers the whole life of a project: land, design, permits, construction, completion, connection and later alterations. Since 2022, building permits across Dubai Municipality, the Dubai Development Authority, Trakhees and DIEZ go through a single unified e-window, with Civil Defence, RTA, DEWA, Etisalat and du linked in.
0846fd8a75222cd4: Durations without a label are from Real Estate Club Dubai. The others are our own planning allowances and depend heavily on the owner's speed of decision. For a closer look at where those months go, see how long it takes to build a villa in Dubai.
4f73135fd39f3f0e: Stage 1: Check the plot before you commit
e4aac1c5fc4276ea: Before you buy, or before you design on a plot you already own, establish what can be built on it. That means the plot affection plan, the master developer's design guidelines, setbacks, height and coverage limits, existing utility connections, access, and any outstanding service charges or developer conditions. Ground conditions and the water table matter too; a basement on a waterfront plot is a very different exercise from one inland.
df3014e9ed175cd6: Who does what: the owner commissions the checks; the consultant interprets planning and design constraints; a UAE-qualified lawyer should review title and any developer agreements. Our guide to plot checks in Dubai goes through them in detail.
e848505fc5727e2e: Stage 2: Set the brief and the budget
9b39691aba5816c3: The brief is the most valuable document in the project and the cheapest to change. Bedrooms, basement or not, pool, staff quarters, home automation, the level of finish, how you will live in the house. Write it down and attach a budget built from the full cost picture, not just a rate per square foot. Our article on what it costs to build a villa in Dubai sets out every line.
2ad87740a592c1cf: Stage 3: Appoint your consultant and design the villa
69e3f3f90b842b71: Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, engineering consultancy in Dubai, including in free zones, may only be practised by registered firms (Law No. 14 of 2025). Your consultant designs the villa across architecture, structure and MEP, prepares the drawings for approval, and normally carries the statutory site role during construction. Dubai Municipality publishes standard contract forms for consultancy and construction on private villas, in Arabic, which are a useful baseline.
0d67345cd19f5db5: The BPS app, relaunched in August 2024, includes a registry and ratings for consultants and contractors, and is worth checking before you appoint. Design normally runs from concept through to detailed design. Every hour spent resolving detail at this stage is cheaper than any hour spent resolving it on site.
acd3e8accf44aaa3: Stage 4: Master-developer NOC and building permit
e18f42899eee3f3e: In a master-planned community, the master developer reviews the design against its guidelines and issues its NOC (no objection certificate). In Nakheel communities, for example, renovation and extension approvals begin with a Nakheel NOC application through its portal before the authority permit.
b87adad7e8de5689: The authority permit then runs through Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. Under Dubai Municipality's published villa procedure, the consultant submits the drawings and fees online, the service-authority NOCs are issued through the unified window, and the permit is issued with stamped drawings (Dubai Municipality). In August 2026, Dubai Municipality announced that it is developing an AI system to check villa applications against the Dubai Building Code, to be piloted with selected consultancies and then rolled out in phases through Build in Dubai over 26 weeks (Dubai Media Office). Until that rollout is complete, plan on the current review process. In practice, cleaner drawings should mean fewer rounds of comments. Our guide to Dubai villa building permits sets out each step, what the owner signs and where the permit stage slips.
3b3e29052ab00dc2: Who does what: the consultant prepares and submits; the master developer and authority review and approve; the owner pays fees and answers design questions quickly.
6b6b28c8699cdf4c: Run a competitive process on a complete design. Your consultant normally prepares the bid package; you, as owner, decide who is invited and who is appointed. Compare bids like-for-like: scope, exclusions, provisional sums, preliminaries, programme, payment terms and retention. The lowest number is not automatically the lowest cost. Our guide to choosing a villa contractor in Dubai explains what to look for, and our guide to villa construction contracts covers the agreement itself. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer before signing.
78f49084b1837dbd: The contractor mobilises, builds and manages the site. The authority inspects at defined stages; Dubai Municipality's procedure refers to staged inspections such as shoring, foundations and slabs. Your consultant fulfils the statutory site role. Monthly valuations measure work done, and you pay against them.
4e6610437dbd8acb: The owner's job during construction is to make decisions on time, approve samples and mock-ups, and keep an independent view of cost and programme. On the contractor's side, we always knew which clients read the monthly report and which did not. The ones who did not were the ones whose sites drifted.
ea5460d38cdac5ba: At the end, Dubai Municipality's procedure describes a joint completion inspection involving Building Control, Survey, telecoms and Civil Defence where needed, followed by the completion certificate and service connection. In parallel, the villa is snagged, defects are listed and rectified, operating manuals and warranties are handed over, and the defects liability period begins. Our villa snagging checklist covers what to inspect.
4184fb9bedaf4d91: Who does what on a Dubai villa build?
3b226a2104cea1bc: Owner: sets the brief and budget, appoints every party, makes decisions, pays.
3a87657461596dff: Owner's representative: represents the owner commercially and practically; cost and programme control, independent site visits and reporting, bid comparison, change control.
328232ebe0acfc80: registered consultant: designs, prepares approval drawings, carries the statutory technical role.
3adaf4b2a6a960d0: Contractor: builds, manages the site, its subcontractors and its programme.
714ea0f97c62f1c1: Master developer: enforces community guidelines and issues its NOC.
fba589c996364d36: Authority: Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits; issues the permit, inspects and issues completion.
f3ce48bdca56dead: How those roles differ, and where they overlap, is covered in owner's representative vs project manager vs consultant.
1436febc0ed78d02: Which decisions cost the most if made late?
2198a914ec5c7f7f: In our experience, these are the decisions that are cheap at design stage and expensive afterwards:
056627216884b190: Basement or no basement. It changes structure, waterproofing, shoring, excavation and programme. Adding one late is effectively a redesign.
714fe8e8945f7253: Overall size and layout. Moving walls after the permit can mean resubmission and lost months.
cd91992e8055b6cd: Glazing and openings. Large-format and structural glazing has long lead times and drives the structure around it.
f13351fba7036b21: MEP strategy. Cooling, home automation, AV and lighting control need their routes and plant space designed in. Adding them later means chasing walls and ceilings.
b744f42c7d7b1af8: Pool and external works. These interact with structure, drainage and levels.
c8dfd0d924572b9d: Finishes and specification. Stone, joinery and sanitaryware chosen late are usually priced as variations, without competition.
126434aa33d3c496: From the builder's side, a late change was rarely a problem for the contractor. It was an opportunity. That is not cynicism, just how the commercial model works.
f0eb62c90428fab3: How do you keep a villa build on programme?
e988fcc181cd18ed: Most delay on a private villa is not caused by bad weather or a shortage of labour. In our experience it comes from information: drawings that arrive late, samples that sit unapproved, questions from site that wait a fortnight for an answer. Three habits make the biggest difference.
01b52dde5d80f264: Agree a decision schedule at the start. List every choice the owner has to make, from tiles to door handles to automation scenes, with the latest date each can be made without holding up the work. Ask the contractor to confirm the dates against its programme.
aa1ea13e1c36490c: Answer site questions quickly. Every request for information from the contractor should have a named person responsible and a target response time. Unanswered questions turn into delay claims.
d4f6a06f5e7a3619: Review progress against the programme monthly, not just against payments. A valuation tells you what has been paid for. The programme tells you whether the villa will be finished when you expect. Both need reading together.
61d8ef2c9a461d62: If you are building from abroad, these habits matter even more, because decisions made by email across time zones take longer. Our guide to building a villa in Dubai from the UK covers how to set this up.
3da501a47fd66188: We sit on the owner's side through every stage, working alongside your registered consultant and your contractor. We help you set the brief and budget, compare bids and choose, then provide independent client-side site visits and progress reporting through to handover. Our villa construction project management service covers the whole journey, and if you are overseas, see our overseas owners page. To talk through your plot, contact us.
abf6136228479095: Real Estate Club Dubai puts design at 3–4 months, approvals at 2–3 months, construction at 8–14 months and snagging at 1–2 months, giving 12–24 months from plot to keys, or 24–36 months for a custom luxury villa.
4c8eca73e3bee6d1: Who applies for the building permit in Dubai?
cb4aaaf794d40f82: Your registered consultant (or in some cases the contractor) submits drawings and fees online through the unified permit window. The owner appoints the consultant and signs off the design, but does not usually make the technical submission.
322c008edbaa9cad: Do I need the master developer's approval before the authority permit?
ef71f2bd1d37fb9a: In master-planned communities, the developer's design guidelines and NOC normally come first. In Nakheel communities, for example, renovation and extension approvals start with a Nakheel NOC application through its portal before the authority permit.
498caa7e0ce810c2: Can I build a villa in Dubai while living overseas?
618731f7e837eb36: Yes, many owners do. It works best when decision-making is planned, with regular reporting and a clear schedule of the choices you need to make and when.
