1021ec225f0b0795: To choose a villa contractor in Dubai, first confirm each bidder is properly registered using official sources, then compare prices only on the same drawings and specification, with preliminaries, provisional sums and exclusions set out side by side. After that, judge the people who will actually run your site, call recent clients, and agree payment terms that follow work done. The cheapest headline figure is rarely the cheapest villa.
169abcaa774d68a4: We spent twenty-one years as the builder before moving to the client's side, so this guide is written from both ends of the table. The twelve questions below are the ones we would want answered before any owner signs.
af1bb4e8c6100347: Before you ask anything: get the basis right
f334f486c51ee34a: Contractor selection goes wrong most often before the first bid arrives. If bidders are pricing from incomplete drawings, a vague specification or different assumptions, you will receive numbers that cannot be compared.
c615403aef4cf93e: Your registered consultant should provide a complete, consistent set of drawings and a specification. Every bidder prices exactly the same thing, on the same form, by the same date. The owner then appoints. Our role at Eastbridge is to help you compare the bids like-for-like and choose, alongside your consultant.
e293fcdec4d4540e: Gooden Heane, Portreath, Cornwall. Built by P Chapman Construction.
0de1271eb073bc64: The 12 questions to ask a villa contractor
4ef7255c2a89be68: 1. Are you registered for this type of work, with this authority?
6d6ce2d7aadd25b3: Do not take a logo on a website as proof. Dubai Municipality's relaunched BPS app includes a search for consultants and contractors registered in Dubai, and lets owners look at information such as a firm's current status and the type and number of projects it is handling. The Build in Dubai platform is the wider gateway for the permit process. Check the trade licence, its expiry date and its licensed activities, and confirm the firm can work under the authority your plot falls within: Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits.
2b8bdfa643f0e831: 2. How many villas like ours are you building right now?
391be273a61b481d: Workload matters as much as track record. A firm with too little work may be under financial pressure; a firm with too much will spread its best people thin. The BPS app's project information is a useful starting point for this conversation.
d3c49334c9422f30: 3. Who will run our site, and can we meet them?
29402c93caec02a6: The site manager or project manager who turns up every day decides the quality of your villa. Ask for names and CVs of the key staff, ask whether they will be dedicated to your project, and ask what happens if they leave. Make the named people a condition of the contract where you can.
11740e2418d3e170: On the contractor's side, we knew that the strongest site manager went to the job with the most demanding client and the best-run paperwork. That is not cynicism; it is how a builder protects its reputation with limited resources.
4af5926923d42f7c: 4. Is your price based on our drawings and specification, with nothing substituted?
3b1b27ad985913cf: Ask every bidder to confirm in writing that they have priced the documents as issued, and to list any alternatives separately. Substituted products and "equivalent" finishes buried in the pricing are a common way of shaving a headline number.
08bfcbf82f4d1a8b: Preliminaries are the cost of running the site rather than building the villa: site staff, welfare, hoarding, temporary power and water, insurance, scaffolding, plant, cleaning and waste. Turner & Townsend put contractor preliminaries in Dubai at 12–14% in 2025 (cited by PRASOON). A bid with preliminaries far below that range is either very efficient or has moved costs elsewhere, or has left them out to be claimed later. Ask for a breakdown, and ask how the monthly figure changes if the programme extends.
82efea7e8c3061f1: 6. What provisional sums have you included, and why?
d75f797a523296e3: A provisional sum is an allowance for work that cannot yet be fully defined. They are legitimate in small numbers. Large or numerous provisional sums mean the true price is still unknown. When comparing bids, list every provisional sum side by side and, where possible, set common figures for all bidders so the comparison is fair.
1c1273ef870bc755: Read exclusions as carefully as the price. Pools, landscaping, external works, kitchens, wardrobes, lighting control, AV, authority fees and service connections are frequently excluded or qualified. Two bids with the same total can be several hundred thousand dirhams apart once exclusions are priced back in.
7b7f2d6d3d9df39b: 8. What is your programme, and what does it depend on?
cf9463ea721df7de: Ask for a programme showing the main stages, the critical path and what the contractor needs from you and when: design information, selections, approvals, payments. A programme that looks fast but depends on you making every decision instantly is not a real programme. See how long it takes to build a villa in Dubai for typical durations.
9ca22c869368ab18: 9. Can we speak to your last three villa clients?
3c82c46e8ed3c158: Not the three the contractor chooses to show off; the last three completed. And call them. Useful questions are: did the final account match the contract price, and if not, why? Was completion on time? How were defects handled after handover? Would you use them again? Whenever you can, visit a finished villa and a live site.
5b158022384c0a93: 10. What payment terms are you asking for?
abd1edb593068d84: Avoid schedules that pay large sums upfront or against calendar dates. Payments should follow work actually completed and checked. Agree how each payment is valued, who checks it and how long you have to pay once it is agreed. Our article on villa construction contracts in the UAE covers how payments are valued in more detail.
7747a6af8bf758f0: 11. What security will you provide: bonds, retention, insurance?
f53a5982231d048c: Ask whether the contractor will provide an advance payment guarantee against any mobilisation payment, a performance bond, and accept retention held back until completion and the end of the defects period. Ask for evidence of contractors' all-risks and third-party insurance. A contractor that resists all of these is telling you something about its balance sheet.
e74659f4f75f3f50: 12. How do you handle changes and delays?
728769a0db524e55: Every villa changes during construction. Ask how the contractor prices variations, how quickly it gives you a cost before carrying out changed work, and how it notifies delays. A clear answer here predicts a calmer project. A vague answer predicts arguments.
cf6d0fa639a8df60: Once the bids are in, put them on one page before anyone looks at the bottom line.
d5b393b6e39652b0: Then hold a short clarification meeting with each serious bidder. Ask the same questions of each, record the answers, and have any changes confirmed in writing before you decide.
0acfd154143c990e: Red flags when choosing a contractor
27984e0bd976ef17: A price far below the others, with no clear explanation.
c8fb38343b1f63db: Pressure to sign quickly, or to pay a deposit before the contract is agreed.
4e6dda5bca162369: Reluctance to name the site team or provide references.
c718f37d978e85b4: Heavy qualifications, long exclusions or "subject to" language throughout the bid.
e1d99e9b548eaa69: Payment schedules weighted to the front of the job.
b4c135e84a916b17: No appetite for bonds, retention or proper insurance.
66320d07271cb963: Suggestions that work can start before the permit is in place.
167ecd229cbfbbf9: A firm that cannot show you a finished villa of comparable quality.
3a00ae91ac7b0719: What a good contractor wants to see from you
c09043b4c6e2f57b: This is the part owners rarely hear. From our years on the builder's side, the best contractors choose their clients as carefully as clients choose them, and they price accordingly.
88a2f5cd34900a72: A good contractor wants to see:
713d9c0cd0f70d15: Complete drawings and a clear specification. Uncertainty is priced as risk. The clearer the documents, the sharper the price.
32e40de6287a7710: A decisive client. Late selections and changing minds are what delay villas. A contractor who sees an organised decision process prices less contingency.
a9997156d061edf9: Proof the money is there. Contractors worry about being paid. Clear payment terms, a sensible cash flow and a track record of paying on time make you a preferred client.
5b3168a32dc1a8e1: A fair contract. One-sided terms do not make a project safer; they make good contractors walk away and leave the bidders who plan to recover their margin through claims.
f3bbda2089d82587: Someone on the client side who understands construction. Contractors prefer dealing with a knowledgeable client representative to dealing with confusion. Disputes are expensive for them too.
656d723c00ba9f97: On the contractor's side, the jobs we priced keenest were the ones where the drawings were finished, the client knew what they wanted, and we trusted we would be paid on time. Those are all things an owner controls.
0bfa8d868878824f: We help owners compare contractor bids like-for-like, question the assumptions behind them and choose with confidence, working alongside your registered consultant. The appointment is always yours. Because we spent two decades pricing work as the builder, we know which parts of a bid hide the risk. 615d1012efcf3b7f: How do I check a contractor is licensed in Dubai?
c5d29c62622e52b2: The Dubai BPS app, relaunched by Dubai Municipality in 2024, includes a search function for consultants and contractors registered in Dubai, and lets owners view information such as current status and the projects firms are handling. Check the trade licence too, and confirm the firm is registered for the type of work and authority your plot falls under.
c79e779533e1bde8: How many contractors should I ask to bid?
87154dd956eb512a: In our experience three to five serious bidders is enough. Fewer gives you no comparison; more wastes everyone's time and the best firms may decline to price a long list.
6ab050e1c36ecc6c: Should I just take the lowest price?
59de6d4afd5fdb3c: Not without normalising the bids first. The lowest headline figure often has the thinnest preliminaries, the largest provisional sums or the longest list of exclusions, and the difference comes back as variations.
d30e5127dce883f1: What payment terms are normal for a villa contractor in Dubai?
a215ac8b2ae8a4f0: Terms vary and are negotiable. The principle to hold to is that payments should follow work actually done and checked on site, with retention held back until completion and defects, rather than a front-loaded schedule tied to calendar dates.

A signed contract with a commencement date secures the job, releases the advance payment and starts the programme clock. If the approvals then ran late, that was not the builder's risk: a crew ready to start, kept off site because the client's permissions were not in place, is a textbook delay and cost claim. Our founder, Philip Chapman, ran P Chapman Construction in the UK for 21 years, and the pattern is the same anywhere: whoever controls the approvals carries the risk of them running late.
3cdaa0adc1568ea7: So on a Nakheel renovation, the sequence we recommend is:
6ec6c35c4a3fec09: Survey and brief. Condition survey and opening-up of the existing villa before the design is fixed.

9ba64c88779e9f36: Tender on the approved drawings. Contractors price what has actually been approved, which removes a whole category of later variations. Our guide on how to choose a villa contractor in Dubai covers the comparison.
29be41d34262f534: Contract with a conditional start. The commencement date is defined as a set number of days after the permit is issued and Nakheel's site requirements are met, not the date of signature.
592ba00d9066c95f: Mobilisation. Deposit paid, Site Access Permit and fence in place, workforce permits issued, then the crew arrives.
2f2902d1784cf55d: If programme pressure means you must appoint the contractor before approvals land, keep the early phase small and defined: surveys, enabling design input, ordering long-lead items you would buy anyway. 7f83f3fa467e617d: On a Dubai villa build, your registered consultant designs the house and carries the statutory technical role, your contractor builds it, and an owner's representative acts solely for you on cost, programme, contract and decisions. A "project manager" can be any of these things depending on who employs them, which is why the title matters less than whose interests the person serves. The roles complement each other; none replaces the consultant.
1a4913b743a9e049: What does each role actually do?
24ac0283ae82eee8: The confusion is understandable. In the UAE, "project manager", "owner's rep", "PMC" and "consultant" are used loosely, and firms describe themselves differently. Focus on function and on who pays them.
0e867e1f9d9cd404: Owner, within professional and statutory duties
3e6864f744a00e56: No; reviews design against brief and budget
6a407bc52dcbc048: Helps the owner compare like-for-like and choose
40abaf5f1c5b57ad: The consultant role is defined by law. Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, only registered consultancies may practise engineering consultancy or present themselves as engineering consultants, and the law applies across Dubai including special development zones and free zones (Law No. 14 of 2025, Dubai Media Office). The other two roles are defined by contract.
ae76874b1df5f6ff: Your consultant is your designer and your statutory technical professional. They take the brief, design the villa, coordinate the engineering, prepare and submit the approval drawings, and normally carry the statutory site role during construction. They are essential. You cannot build without one. Dubai Municipality publishes standard consultancy contract forms for private villas, in Arabic, and the BPS app lists registered consultants with ratings.
4ae195227a1d9a4a: "Project manager" describes an activity, not an allegiance. A contractor has project managers. Some consultants offer project management as an add-on. Some independent firms offer it to owners. The work is planning, coordinating, chasing and reporting. Before you rely on a project manager, ask who appoints them and who pays them.
f7d9bb543ccb8306: An owner's representative manages the project from the owner's side of the table only. Typical scope: setting and controlling the budget, the programme and the decision schedule; helping the owner compare bids and choose; reviewing valuations and variations; independent client-side site visits and reporting; and keeping the consultant and contractor accountable to the brief. The owner's representative does not design, does not make authority submissions and does not take on the consultant's statutory role. The value lies in having no stake in the design fee or the construction price.
97d78aa2f79c2f57: Owers House, Feock, Cornwall. Built by P Chapman Construction.
c8d73c20a5a75653: Where are the conflicts of interest?
999b106841209b05: Every party on a villa build has a legitimate commercial interest. Conflicts arise when one party is asked to check its own work.
f3ff61bd1b788d22: Design-and-build firms. One company designs, prices and builds. That can be efficient, with a single point of responsibility. But the same firm decides how much building the design contains, prices it, and then prices every change. Nobody independent is testing whether the design is efficient or the price is fair, unless you arrange it.
157dc0ce87b8dc04: Consultants checking their own design. When the consultant who designed the villa also reviews the contractor's claims for design-related changes, they are judging, in part, their own drawings. Most consultants handle this professionally. But a variation caused by a design gap is a difficult thing for the designer to call. In August 2025, Dubai Municipality warned villa consultancies about over-designing structures and inflating build costs (Gulf News). A design that is heavier than it needs to be is expensive, and a second, independent look is the simplest way to test it.
737e9f995a41bc40: Fees tied to construction value. Consultant fees in Dubai are commonly a percentage of construction cost. That is market practice, not wrongdoing, but it means the fee structure itself does not reward making the building cheaper.
9d7a69a4207f2f2f: Contractor-employed project managers. The contractor's project manager is there to deliver the contractor's job profitably. That is their job. It is not the same job as protecting your budget.
fffb61199f1fd3b1: Anyone who has run a building company knows the pattern: projects where the client has no independent adviser are commercially easier for the contractor. Provisional sums go unquestioned, variation rates go untested and monthly valuations are rarely challenged. Nobody is doing anything wrong. There is simply no one asking.
4eee4187fb2c559f: Whatever you call the role, put it in writing. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on the final form.

03cac42ba396a845: When do you need an owner's representative, and when don't you?
e9b1306704d55409: To be straightforward about it, not every villa needs one.
b1fc51fc1b38528c: You probably do not need one if the villa is relatively simple, the design is complete before pricing, you have built before, you live in Dubai, you have time to attend site and read the monthly reports, and you trust your consultant to act firmly on your behalf with the contractor. 4fc46f36a9a95659: What should you ask before appointing an owner's representative?
2e66d2b78dc94277: If you decide you want one, test the fit before you sign. These are the questions we would ask in your position:
fb3dca9e81f677df: Who else pays you on this project? The only acceptable answer is nobody. Ask whether they receive referral fees, commissions or any other benefit from consultants, contractors or suppliers.
530954d442a9eb54: What have you built, and from which side? Experience on the contractor's side, the consultant's side or the developer's side gives different strengths. Ask for specifics, and be wary of anyone who claims experience they cannot describe in detail.
c6959a4cff9066bb: What exactly will you deliver each month? A sample report tells you more than a brochure.
e0cd224180fb3072: How often will you be on site, and who will come? Agree the frequency and the person, not just the firm.
1ded210355b1f85b: What will you not do? A good owner's representative is clear about the boundary with your registered consultant, and will not claim to design, make authority submissions or take on the consultant's statutory role.
91d9ca49b363df59: How is the fee structured? A fixed or time-based fee against a defined scope keeps incentives cleaner than a percentage of construction value.
0131cad73515fa12: An honest answer to the last question often tells you more than the others.

6c0c9b6955954a1d: What hidden problems do older Palm villas have?
80f5e14c4ecfe31b: Many of the original frond villas are now around two decades old. They were built quickly, at scale, in a demanding marine environment. In our experience the same issues come up again and again on coastal houses of that age, wherever they are.
40bfd2d449bb25d5: Roof membranes, wet-room tanking, terraces over habitable rooms and basement waterproofing all have a finite life. Failures often show as staining, blistering paint or musty rooms long after the damage has started. Replacing a roof or basement membrane is not a cosmetic job; it means stripping finishes, possibly lifting screeds, and doing it before any new interior goes in.
8c8c664a32558cf2: Air-conditioning systems, ductwork, pipework and electrical distribution installed when the villa was built may be near the end of their life or undersized for how you want to live now. If you are replacing finishes, it is almost always cheaper to replace tired services at the same time than to open the villa up again in three years.
4dcef86afbeec19b: Wind-borne salt attacks external metalwork, fixings, balustrades, window frames, AC condensers and, in the worst cases, reinforcement in concrete where the cover has been compromised. Cracking and rust staining on external concrete need investigating by a structural engineer, not painting over.
24f78288401bceb9: Pools on older villas commonly have leaking shells, failed tiling and outdated plant. A pool is a structure, and a rebuild sits firmly in the approvals column. One published Dubai cost guide puts new pool construction at AED 80k–250k, which is a useful reality check if the pool is on your list.
495388774126685c: On the contractor's side, the first thing we priced on any refurbishment of an older coastal house was the risk in the envelope. Interiors are predictable. Roofs, basements and anything facing the sea are not, and an honest contractor will tell you so.

69efedc8513f8049: What are the budget traps on a Palm renovation?
3fb8ba961731b05e: The traps are rarely dramatic. They are small decisions that compound.
224cf17954dc1dca: Provisional sums for the unknown. If the bid carries a modest provisional sum for "waterproofing repairs" or "MEP remedials", the real cost is still unknown. Push for investigation before signing, or at least a clear rate.
a553424ab8ac9d84: Specification drift. Upgrading a finish here and a fitting there feels small. Across a whole villa it is not. Agree a specification and track every change against it.

29d65ce1cc1a78da: Programme slippage. Every extra month is another month of preliminaries, another month of rent if you have moved out, and another month before you can use the house.

Narrow frond roads and shared access make logistics harder than on an open plot.
bc48105c1ed81053: Two practical points. First, a contractor who has not priced for these constraints will either cut corners or come back for more money. 83a5692ca06750ec: Should I renovate or rebuild my Palm villa?
3f8694085f101503: This is the question owners least want to ask, and the one that most often needs asking.
d3bb43c96963696b: Renovation makes sense when the structure is sound, the layout broadly works, and your brief is mainly about finishes, kitchens, bathrooms, services and outdoor space. Rebuild deserves serious consideration when the brief keeps expanding towards new structure, a reworked envelope, full services replacement and significant extensions. At that point you can end up paying for much of a new house while still working within the constraints of the old one, and carrying the risk of whatever the existing structure is hiding.
17e82f7699b2164a: Our rule of thumb: once the renovation scope starts to look like a new building, get both routes priced properly by your consultant before committing. From the builder's side, we know how a stalled job looks from the contractor's chair, and what an incoming builder needs before it will price the rest. This is what we would want any owner to do, in order.

be582da7cc67af10: The contractor's cash flow is under strain, on your job or across its business
273a9351de0348b3: Have all valued payments been made, and is the contractor paying its own supply chain?
67f0f214b8438518: Work stopped in one area, waiting
095c9ecc190182db: Missing or late design information, or an unmade owner decision
5aec517345180512: Is there an outstanding request for information or selection, and whose is it?
ccd0201cd3944bbf: A formal letter about suspension or delay
a4d5b2216abd0d08: A dispute about payment, variations or time
b8d127b472cd8136: What does the contract say about notices, suspension and extensions?
9b09c8416fa53df7: Contractor over-committed elsewhere, or deliberately slowing to force a negotiation
48e484044286e165: What does the programme say, and when was it last updated?
a7085ffdb2a4f008: A dispute between owner and consultant, or a consultant stretched too thin
a6bfa826888352c7: Is the consultant's appointment and fee position in order?
51eead247393a0d9: Abandonment, insolvency or a serious dispute
44899cfabb7dec25: Has the contractor responded in writing, and is it still trading?
2cee00b3db0226bb: On the builder's side, a slowing site was almost always a cash signal before it was a programme signal. Labour goes first, then the subcontractors stop returning calls, then the letters start. An owner who notices the first stage and asks the right questions early has far more options than one who waits for the letter.

39323ef0eebe91b7: What should I do in the first ten days?
5f8ec5b08df349e7: The checklist below is the order we recommend. It is deliberately conservative: nothing in it closes off an option, and everything in it improves your position whichever route you choose.
ec7d83d3831f64d1: Visit, photograph and video the whole site, dated
19641d5b27745ba7: Fixes the state of the works before anything is moved, removed or disputed
3cb48bae3ac9f9b0: Check site security, hoarding, safety and weather protection
229f2172c6184adf: An open, unprotected site deteriorates and creates liability
49c8601af73a38fd: Write to the contractor asking for the reason and a return date
f341147af35e7dbc: Puts the position on record and invites a reply you can rely on
f2608cb9ec2a1d55: Gather the contract, drawings, programme, valuations, payments and correspondence
da54af283d034c2c: You cannot assess anything you cannot find
a561b9d1edd63725: Pause further payments until the position is checked
d03b4f605cbf7d1a: Money paid ahead of work is leverage lost
c0dd1627c2807857: Read the termination, suspension, notice and dispute clauses with a lawyer
ac34c624dd4c150e: A wrongful termination can turn a strong position into a weak one
74f7f8199e3740a7: Confirm the permit, insurance and bond position
146ad009b3f248c7: Expiring cover or guarantees cannot be recovered later
3624c886dba2a637: Ask your consultant for a technical assessment of progress and quality
aa06af32773f7942: It is the basis of any restart, renegotiation or changeover
6b581eebc7e98955: Reconcile what has been paid against what has been built
3f911f80422646c3: Tells you whether you are ahead of or behind the work
b5533b0d3de349b4: Estimate the cost and time to complete, and set out the options
9bbcdbe5f026d3c8: Turns a crisis into a decision
6dced5fbb587d8f0: Days 1–2: secure the site and the record
170d795cb6cb196e: Go to site, or send someone you trust. Photograph and video every room, elevation and service run, with dates. Note what materials are on site and what plant has been removed. Check the hoarding, access control, temporary power and water, and anything open to the weather, such as unprotected roof membranes, exposed reinforcement or stored finishes. Under many contracts these risks sit with the contractor while it is in possession of the site, but a deteriorating building is your problem whoever pays for it.
efad380ae81e448a: Days 2–3: pause the money, not the conversation
a10381103b847bec: Keep talking to the contractor, politely and in writing. Ask why work has stopped and when it will resume. But pause any payment not yet properly valued until you know where you stand. Pay only what has been properly valued and approved under the contract for work actually done, and take legal advice before withholding anything the contract says is due, because an unjustified non-payment can hand the contractor a right to suspend.
325cdef45488fa44: On the contractor's side, the request we dreaded most from a client was not an angry phone call. It was a calm letter asking for an updated programme, a list of outstanding information and a reconciliation of the account. Those three documents show quickly who is really behind.
fe353d367ad52862: Days 3–5: read the contract before acting on it
afb7a0cc598de19a: Find the clauses on suspension, termination, notices, extensions of time, liquidated damages, retention, bonds and disputes. Notice periods matter: many contracts require a notice of default and a period to remedy it before termination is possible. This is general information, not legal advice; your contract and UAE law decide what you can do, so take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer at this point, not after you have sent a termination letter. Our guide to villa construction contracts in the UAE explains the main mechanisms, and if the dispute is about variations or time, see how we help with variations, delays and claims.
f1fee7d73935dd2e: Check three time-sensitive items at the same time: whether the building permit and its conditions remain in order (ask your consultant), whether the contractor's all-risks and liability insurance is still in force, and when any performance bond or advance payment guarantee expires. A bond that lapses during a dispute protects no one.
19b2b360d1498997: Days 5–8: establish what has actually been built
3057809c673900ed: Ask your registered consultant for a technical assessment of the stage of the works and whether they conform to the permit and the approved drawings. Alongside it, reconcile the money: total valued, total paid, retention held, variations agreed and variations claimed. Compare that with what is physically in place. If the payments have run ahead of the work, you need to know by how much.
627fbc974e03cf6b: Days 7–10: cost to complete, and the options
6a958ef6db4c7bf8: With the record and the reconciliation in hand, estimate what it will cost and how long it will take to finish. Then set out the options side by side: bring the current contractor back with a recovery programme, renegotiate scope or terms, or replace the contractor. A changeover carries real costs in time, re-pricing and risk.
a669dcbfda948830: Not in the first ten days, and not without legal advice. Termination is sometimes right, but it is a legal step with consequences, and a contractor that has been terminated wrongly may have a claim against you.
de9a7cb2670d54f1: For context, a Gulf News legal column published in 2024 describes the general position under Article 877 of the UAE Civil Transactions Law: where a contractor performs defectively or contrary to the agreement, the owner may require it to put matters right within a reasonable time and, if it fails, may ask the court to cancel the contract or to authorise completion by another contractor at the first contractor's expense. How that applies to your contract is a question for a UAE-qualified lawyer.
9ac2da9118a8486b: How do I change contractor on a Dubai villa?
d7052453f1c187c7: Dubai Municipality's Administrative Resolution No. 10 of 2019 sets out the procedures for replacing an engineering consultant or a contractor on applications made to the municipality. In summary, as the English translation on the Dubai Legislation Portal describes it (the Arabic text prevails):
aebfbd1ba95647af: With the outgoing contractor's agreement: your engineering consultant submits the application, signed by the consultant and the outgoing contractor, with a declaration from the owner approving the change and, where a permit has been issued, the consultant's technical report on the stage of the works and their conformity with the permit and approved plans.
728b90a3cb475a66: Without its agreement: the consultant submits the application with the owner's declaration, the reasons for the change and the technical report. The municipality notifies the outgoing contractor, which has five working days to give its reasons and its own technical report. If it does not respond, the municipality proceeds. Where the dispute is financial or contractual, the municipality proceeds with the replacement; where it is technical, the municipality verifies the issues first.
985f5db13cb9ec05: In both cases: the replacement contractor must be licensed, with a classification not lower than the building requires, and may not start work until a new building permit is issued in its name, on payment of the prescribed fees and security.
e2a0e39c5b66bb08: Dubai Municipality publishes a request form for changing a consultant or contractor, with and without agreement, and its online building permit system includes the change of consultant or contractor among its services. Your consultant makes the application, through the Build in Dubai platform or the authority's own system. If your permit was issued by Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority rather than Dubai Municipality, the route may differ, so ask your consultant to confirm the procedure for your plot. In communities with a master developer, check whether the developer's own approvals also need updating.
f3cda5ea74d064f5: What about a stalled villa in Abu Dhabi?
07a44505503809d0: The principles are the same: secure the site, preserve the record, pause unvalued payments, take legal advice and establish what has been built. The procedure is not. In Abu Dhabi the Department of Municipalities and Transport regulates private villas and permits are handled by the municipalities through TAMM. Ask your consultant to confirm the current requirements for changing a contractor on your permit before you commit to a changeover.
dfc1aee4be052f15: What does an incoming contractor need to price the rest fairly?
fbdc7a5aea7f5c70: An incoming contractor prices the unknown first: work it cannot see, quality it cannot verify, materials it cannot account for and paperwork it does not have. Every unknown goes into the price as risk.
933bf16fa6b956a9: An incoming contractor prices more keenly when it receives:
9cd70a7db72078ec: A dated photographic and written record of the works in place, including concealed work recorded before it was covered, where it exists.
c4738cbe2f3eb406: The consultant's technical report on progress and conformity.
114659ab2473b263: A defects list, so the new contractor is not later blamed for, or paid twice for, the previous contractor's work.
f88498749440a2a7: An inventory of materials and equipment on site, with ownership confirmed.
7c88c2f97120e56d: The current drawings, specification and outstanding design information, with nothing left open that can be closed.
4351af7afb7d47ee: A clear scope to complete, separating remedial work from new work.
e4231a3c7511f32c: Without that pack, a recovery price carries every doubt as contingency. With it, the job can usually restart at a fair price.
180f6a9b95c7b040: What mistakes make a stalled villa worse?
00e1877ddd52cf10: Paying an advance or a "goodwill" sum to get labour back, with no change to the programme or the terms.
c351781589888894: Terminating by email in frustration, before checking notice provisions and taking legal advice.
0df305cceb96d018: Letting another builder start work before the change is approved and a new permit is in place.
8e830292c2ad67be: Allowing the outgoing contractor to remove materials or equipment without an agreed inventory.
cdf34a5551cb3699: Letting the bond, the insurance or the defects record lapse while attention is on the argument.
f7592eacd637069f: Agreeing a new price for "finishing" without separating remedial work from incomplete work.
6a608cad4871584a: Most of these come from the same instinct: wanting the site busy again quickly. A week spent establishing the facts usually saves months later.

d07b6cf7ec069d6b: What should I do if my villa contractor stops work in Dubai?
1be3ddf45ac520ff: Photograph and record the site, write to the contractor asking for the reason and a date to return, pause any payment not yet properly valued until the position is checked, and ask your registered consultant for an assessment of progress and quality. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer before withholding sums the contract says are due or terminating the contract.
40027e5532403b59: Can I change contractor halfway through a villa build in Dubai?
91b77941d3630cad: Yes. Where Dubai Municipality issued the permit, its Administrative Resolution No. 10 of 2019 sets out procedures for replacing a contractor both with and without the outgoing contractor's consent. The engineering consultant submits the application with an owner's declaration and, where a permit has been issued, a technical report on the stage and conformity of the works. If your permit came from Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, ask your consultant to confirm the procedure.
341bf5a75e888953: What if the outgoing contractor refuses to agree to the change?
0a4ec8fa03d95e82: Under the resolution, Dubai Municipality notifies the outgoing contractor, who has five working days to respond with its reasons and a technical report. 847ea269ae848aaf: How long does it take to restart a stalled villa?
fbbef1f2a5143de2: It depends on the cause, the state of the works and whether the current contractor can be brought back. 6f194a245df295de: Should I keep paying the contractor while the site is stopped?

dbc3887f7d72bb3e: Is there a standard villa construction contract in Dubai?
162ec8e49c20219f: Dubai Municipality publishes two guidance contract forms for private villas: one for engineering consultancy services and one for construction contracting. DM's stated aim is to strengthen contractual relationships between owners, consultants and contractors and reduce the disputes that delay projects.
83b96e8bb70b0cb7: The forms are currently available in Arabic only.
45912407c03d9ba4: They are for guidance and not mandatory.
eac775dae8f0b1cd: The parties may amend them by agreement.
63b11ab1c0a96613: They are a sensible starting point, and the forms can be downloaded from Dubai Municipality. If you do not read Arabic, get a reliable translation and have any amendments reviewed by a UAE-qualified lawyer. The Arabic text will normally be the one that counts.
f683e93de64baf28: Your consultant's appointment matters too. Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, engineering consultancy across Dubai, including free zones, is regulated, and only registered consultancies may practise as engineering consultants. Make sure the contract and the consultant's appointment fit together: who approves what, who values payments, who issues instructions.

01d4237bf0e1c82e: This is the first thing to establish, because it decides who carries the risk of quantities.
e853f242fa5bf12d: Fixed price for a defined scope
df171607c41942fe: Agreed rates applied to measured quantities
ce7423001c09f5ff: Higher, if the scope is complete
5a87e78bb7c8c4d6: Lower until the work is measured
ffd3c02d12b0c744: Work that cannot be fully defined at the start
9ac53bb589369be4: A lump sum is only as fixed as the scope behind it. If the drawings are incomplete, the "fixed" price will move through variations. Many villa contracts are a blend: a lump sum for most of the work, with remeasurable elements such as excavation or piling, plus provisional sums. Know which items sit where.
5a63fb0faa6740b4: How should payments be valued and approved?
50e83327c9d47830: Payments should follow work done, not the calendar. A sound process looks like this:
78ea122999fc0b1d: The contractor submits a monthly application showing work completed and materials on site.
effe345b39891607: The owner's consultant checks it against progress on site and the contract rates.
8626599be659b29a: The approved amount is issued, less retention and any agreed deductions.
b9cece76d309806d: The owner pays within the period the contract sets.
16de57905bb0c875: Owners get into trouble when they pay against a contractor's application without it being checked, or when the payment schedule is front-loaded so that the contractor is paid ahead of the work. Once you have overpaid, your leverage on quality and completion is gone.
f20e27d6e8786ee1: Retention, advance payments and performance bonds
c3f99e67a26d7e09: These are the owner's main forms of financial security.
1008041a3457fae5: Retention is a percentage held back from each payment. Typically part is released at completion and the balance at the end of the defects liability period. It gives the contractor a reason to return and fix defects.
261e0df3ac12ae33: Advance payment guarantee. If you pay a mobilisation advance, it should be secured by a bank guarantee for the same amount, reducing as the advance is recovered from later payments.
c7caaf343c4197cf: Performance bond. A bank guarantee, often a percentage of the contract value, that the owner can call on if the contractor fails to perform. Check its wording, its expiry date and the conditions for calling it. A bond that expires before completion protects no one.
69cec325df720d16: Ask also for evidence of contractors' all-risks and third-party liability insurance for the duration of the works.
2aa5396dec9e3276: How do variations work in a villa contract?
8d67b6ed9b33ca54: A variation is any change to the work described in the contract: an added room, a different finish, a moved wall, an omission. Variations are normal. Unmanaged variations are the single biggest cause of budget overruns we have seen.
747fd32c06f98f04: A good variation procedure has four steps:
efe374166640755d: Instruction in writing. Only the person named in the contract can instruct a change, and only in writing.
1245925677cf86c1: Quotation before work. The contractor prices the change, including any effect on time, before carrying it out.
de975e63d6c5f62a: Agreement. The owner accepts, rejects or negotiates the cost and time.
d1483afa7ae4a702: Record. The agreed variation is logged and carried into the next payment and the running final account.
c6a0d5a20ef9b36e: On the contractor's side, we learned early that verbal instructions were where margin was made or lost. A client who asked for "just a small change" on a site walk, without paper, would see it reappear later at a price and with a time claim attached. Insisting on written instructions protects both sides.
03c08184b2f727d7: Keep a variation register: number, description, date instructed, quoted cost, agreed cost, time effect, status. Review it monthly against the budget.
fe0c060abfbcce9f: Extension of time and liquidated damages, in plain English
bce4c2b0289f517c: These two clauses work as a pair.
755609dcbda9336c: Liquidated damages (LDs) are a sum the contractor pays for each day or week the villa is late beyond the completion date. They are agreed in advance so the owner does not have to prove the actual loss of a late handover. How they are treated is a matter of UAE law, including whether a court or tribunal may adjust them, so take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on your specific clause.
f5fb5658cd61adf2: Extension of time (EOT) moves the completion date when the delay is caused by something the contract says is not the contractor's risk: owner changes, late information from the owner's side, authority delays outside the contractor's control, or other listed events. If an EOT is granted, the contractor is not liable for LDs for that period.
fa6ae3415bf0d49f: A well-drafted contract also sets out:
6498908cb83b3052: Notice periods. The contractor must notify a delay event within a set time.
fd57343254eee43b: Substantiation. The notice should be followed by details of cause, effect and evidence.
c83233ea96b6d24e: Assessment. The person named in the contract assesses the claim within a set period.
b86d1073752bea32: Loss and expense. Whether the contractor can recover additional cost, such as extended preliminaries, as well as time.
aaa25b3a0776f7db: From two decades of preparing and answering EOT claims under JCT contracts and through adjudication, our view is that the outcome is decided by the programme and the records, not the rhetoric. A claim supported by an updated programme, dated correspondence and site records is hard to resist. A rejection with no evidence behind it is equally hard to defend.
86cb0096d12ded34: What does good contract administration look like?
2cb20869e256e8ed: This is where we draw most directly on two decades on the builder's side. The projects that ended well shared the same habits:
a4dddada3d6c8610: A baseline programme agreed at the start, updated monthly, with the critical path shown.
b36f52d195ad64a4: Weekly site records: labour and plant on site, work done, weather, instructions received, problems encountered, with photographs.
5331d8bcda310f73: Minuted progress meetings with actions and owners, issued within days.
89599ba6f153eff9: One instruction route. All changes in writing through the named person.
82206002de648044: A live variation register and cost report, reviewed against budget every month.
27569a3ef562d312: Notices dealt with on time, by both sides, every time.
f8ae754ea4e1629b: Correspondence filed so it can be found a year later.
80ef28fabf54084c: None of this is glamorous. All of it decides who wins an argument about time and money.
e8d9ae7bf7171f53: How are villa construction disputes resolved?
4fb5fab895e22930: In general terms, most contracts provide for a sequence: negotiation between the parties, sometimes escalation to senior representatives or mediation, then a binding route such as arbitration or the courts, depending on what the contract says. The UK statutory adjudication regime that many British owners know does not apply in the same way in the UAE. The right route, the time limits and the costs depend on your contract and on UAE law, so take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer early. The cheapest dispute is the one prevented by good records. b6a8622b308cc78c: The contractor's rate normally covers the building itself: substructure, frame, envelope, internal fit-out to the specified standard, and the mechanical, electrical and plumbing installations. It also includes the contractor's preliminaries, the cost of running the site. Turner & Townsend put contractor preliminaries in Dubai at 12–14% (as cited by PRASOON), so a meaningful slice of every square foot is site management, welfare, temporary works, insurance and plant rather than the building you will live in.
13bd7687bd2977c0: What is usually outside the rate:
7434b5ef73769d09: Design and engineering fees for the architect and engineers
88a3ddfc5e3c4c4d: Swimming pool and external works, unless specifically included
d49c9cfb163ff669: Furniture, fixtures and equipment (FF&E), and often specialist items such as home automation, lighting control, audio-visual and wine rooms

A bespoke luxury villa sits firmly at the percentage end.
bec9a5bacc616523: Your consultant must be registered with Dubai Municipality. 4f6d1f1aa83a58bb: Real Estate Club Dubai puts permits, NOCs and DEWA connection at AED 25k–75k, or 2–5% of build cost. b36794a7179b61f1: Real Estate Club Dubai gives a pool range of AED 80k–250k, landscaping at AED 100–500 per sq ft of garden, and FF&E at 30–40% of build cost at the top end of the market. FF&E is the line owners most often forget, and on a luxury villa it can be one of the largest.

781038aa86b2350d: Here is a worked example using the published ranges above. It is illustrative, not a quotation. We assume 10,000 sq ft of built-up area, luxury specification at AED 900–1,400 per sq ft (Engel & Völkers), and 4,000 sq ft of landscaped garden. For authority charges we use the top of the fixed range as a floor and 2% of build as a prudent ceiling; that is our own rule of thumb for a villa this size.
a3452cf0d3fbed50: The arithmetic is simple; the point is the spread. Construction is roughly 69–82% of the total before FF&E, and less again once furniture is added. If you only budget the per-square-foot rate, you are budgeting perhaps two thirds of the project.
0631d434e3aa2b39: The range is also wide because the low column pairs the cheapest assumptions together and the high column the most expensive. adb6e264cc8c38cb: Our founder spent 21 years running a premium building company whose houses won RIBA and LABC recognition. From that seat, budgets almost never failed on the rate. They failed on the gaps around it.
0865c294a9d29b34: Provisional sums. When a design is incomplete, the contractor carries an allowance for the unknown item: a kitchen, a staircase, a lighting system. The allowance is often set low so the overall bid looks competitive. When the real item is chosen, the difference becomes an addition. On the contractor's side, a bid with a lot of provisional sums was always a bid with a lot of room in it, for us.
cf7b8e0b455e013a: Late decisions. A change on paper costs a drawing revision. The same change after the slab is poured costs demolition, re-work, a programme delay and the contractor's time-related site costs for every extra week. Finishes, sanitaryware, glazing systems and automation chosen late are the most common culprits.
c9561ca180496839: Variations priced without competition. Once a contractor is appointed, every change is priced by one firm, with no competing bid to keep it honest. Variation rates are often higher than the rates in the original price.
80e33c25a9c4c2bc: Over-design. In August 2025, Dubai Municipality warned villa consultancies about over-designing structures and inflating build costs (Gulf News). An over-specified frame or foundation is cost you pay for without seeing it.
ab9aadc66e10549b: Delay. Every extra month on site means another month of the contractor's preliminaries. With preliminaries at 12–14% of the contract (Turner & Townsend, via PRASOON), a long overrun is expensive before a single extra brick is laid. Published fee figures for renovation permits vary widely, so ask your consultant to set out the actual charges for your scope.

50749c4fe5d744bc: External works. Smart Renovation puts outdoor, pool and landscaping work at AED 50,000–200,000 combined; a pool rebuild alone can use much of that.
09e234f95557ba57: Furniture, AV, lighting control and automation, which are often outside the main contract.

d703387bf4c6a688: Always read the contractor's exclusions before you compare totals. On a renovation, the exclusions list often says more about the price than the price does.

7891d05553657663: The result is well above Smart Renovation's whole-villa mid-range band of AED 400,000–800,000. On building works alone (AED 1.5–2.7 million), the example sits between Property Finder's five-bedroom full upgrade (AED 0.9–1.4 million) and its luxury structural band (AED 1.5–3.5 million or more). Those belong to the hidden costs below.
aa4ba66dc0e431bb: What are the three hidden costs in older villas?
d9d26f81b0d3504f: Our founder, Philip Chapman, ran P Chapman Construction, a premium residential builder in the UK, for 21 years. From the builder's side, the renovation budgets that failed almost never failed on the rates. They failed on three things the original price did not capture.
c4bc9602b588e811: A new build is priced from drawings. A renovation is priced from what can be seen, and in an older villa the expensive parts usually cannot be.
c30704b90c750954: Waterproofing. Roof membranes, terraces over rooms, wet-room tanking and basements all have a finite life. Failure shows late, as staining, blistering paint or a musty room, long after the damage started. Replacing a membrane means stripping finishes and often lifting screeds, before any new interior goes in.
d6a1f344e5ec14cd: Services. Air conditioning, ductwork, pipework and electrical distribution installed when the villa was built may be near the end of its life, or undersized for how you want to live now. In Dubai the cooling system is the heart of the house, and replacing it is a building project, not a fitting.
f1b58238f1aac8f2: Concrete and salt. In coastal communities, wind-borne salt attacks metalwork, fixings, frames and, where concrete cover is poor, reinforcement. Cracking and rust staining need a structural engineer's view, not paint.
339dffd4fd137188: On the contractor's side, the first thing we priced on any refurbishment was the risk in the envelope and the services. Interiors are predictable; roofs, basements and plant are not. When the information was thin, we priced what we could see and knew the rest would come back as variations, priced by one firm with no competition. That is the single biggest reason renovation budgets move.
7bc1860035b33266: Renovations spread. Move a bathroom and you need new drainage falls, new waterproofing and new screeds. Open up a wall and the electrics behind it no longer suit the new layout. Replace the air-conditioning units and the ducts, controls, condensate routes and electrical supply may all need to follow. Lay new flooring on one level and the thresholds, doors and stairs no longer line up.
0fd406eb0944ba80: There is also the regulatory knock-on. The Dubai Building Code applies to building designs permitted after it came into force (Decree No. 45 of 2021), and the code itself describes its application to the renovation, modification and addition of existing buildings. In practice, new work in an older villa is designed to today's rules, not the rules the house was built under. Your consultant will tell you what that means for your scope; it is better to know at concept stage than at permit stage.
5dcbf5c91f2eb9bd: In our experience, a brief that starts as "kitchen, bathrooms and finishes" and ends as "most of the services and half the screeds" is the norm in older villas, not the exception. Price the knock-ons at design stage and they are decisions. Discover them on site and they are variations.
53d0ed8518b5039c: Every extra month on a renovation costs you three ways. The contractor's preliminaries, the cost of running the site, continue: Turner & Townsend put preliminaries in Dubai at 12–14% of contract value (cited by PRASOON). Your rent and storage continue if you have moved out. And the house is unusable for another month.
e14c291c654144f1: Time is lost in predictable places: discoveries that need redesign, late decisions on finishes, design changes after the NOC that need resubmitting, and long-lead items such as glazing, joinery and imported stone ordered too late. Published guides put larger projects with structural work at six months or more on site, before approvals.
0ea08aa75598de41: Living in the villa during the works rarely saves money once services, waterproofing or structure are involved. The contractor has to phase the job around you, protect occupied rooms and work slower, and you pay for all of it in preliminaries.
81b0156981169965: How do you keep a villa renovation on budget?
e0c888ea93e95a9d: Survey before you design. Commission a proper condition survey of roofs, wet areas, basement, pool and MEP, and open up small areas where it matters. It is the cheapest money on the project.
e7cb9f2b7e7955e1: Price the design at concept stage. Get an early cost check before the drawings are finished, so the brief and budget can be adjusted while it is cheap to do so.
195abea8518964de: Turn provisional sums into scope. If the bid carries an allowance for "waterproofing repairs" or "MEP remedials", the real cost is still unknown. Investigate before signing, or at least agree rates.
836035799af4ac4b: Compare bids like-for-like. Normalise exclusions, allowances and preliminaries before looking at totals. Our guide to choosing a villa contractor in Dubai explains how.
ee024417230bd26a: Hold the contingency yourself. Release it by decision, not by default.
2fe722063cf5346b: Price every change before it is instructed. Cost and time, in writing, first.
8f02cb4afc1e3bfe: Decide early, order early. Finishes and long-lead items fixed before work starts protect the programme.
4ae0324a2e2dc86d: Read the contract. See villa construction contracts in the UAE, and take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer.
bc9ea039f34fb55c: If the scope keeps growing towards new structure, a new envelope and full services replacement, stop and price a rebuild properly alongside it. Our Palm Jumeirah renovation guide covers that decision and the approvals sequence, and our guide to what it costs to build a villa in Dubai gives the new-build comparison.
498c3292274599eb: For an indicative figure on your own villa, our villa build and renovation cost calculator applies the published whole-villa renovation bands by scope and lists its sources. Because those bands do not scale with floor area, it will read low for a large or older villa like the worked example above; use the per square foot approach here for those.

fcbfc6627dcd5b62: Handover · 25 October 2026 · Updated 29 October 2026 · 7 min read · By Philip Chapman
4a6c72d8a9c2dfdc: Snag the systems first (waterproofing, AC, drainage, pool, electrics), because cosmetic defects are cheap to fix and system defects are not.
4d39eeb18a8b8c72: Test things under load: run every AC unit, fill every bath, flush every drain and leave the pool circulating before you sign anything.
4eb050d1defce0a3: Do not accept handover without the completion certificate, as-built drawings, warranties and O&M manuals in hand or on a dated list.
f73e22ee7ff373c2: Retention and the final payment are your leverage; once they are released, snag lists tend to stall.

f8b73fa9ad21071f: When should you snag a new villa?
9377e25b55084678: What documents should you collect at handover?
c14ac01dcfb7e4e8: How snag lists get closed out, and how they stall
c3cbc3e6a7f41d83: Snagging a new villa in Dubai means testing every system under real conditions and inspecting every finish before you accept the keys, then holding enough leverage to get the defects fixed. Start with waterproofing, air conditioning, drainage, the pool and electrics, because those are expensive to put right later. Collect the completion certificate, as-built drawings, warranties and operation and maintenance manuals before you sign off.
cbbecd4eded530ac: Below is the checklist we use, followed by the documents to collect and the contractor's view of how snag lists get closed or stalled.
2a402e8eda679b6c: When should you snag a new villa?
b34c0e462835b253: Snagging comes at the end of construction, after the authority's completion inspection and before you formally accept the villa. In Dubai, the residential permit process ends with a joint completion inspection involving Building Control and other bodies, followed by a completion certificate and service connection (Dubai Municipality). A completion certificate tells you the building meets the authority's requirements. It does not tell you the grout is clean, the shower drains or the AC holds temperature in August.
1f8eb62ad877889f: Published guidance allows around one to two months for snagging (Real Estate Club Dubai). In our experience, the realistic sequence is:
3cf670dbcdb5966b: Pre-handover inspection by the owner's side, with a written, numbered snag list.
5838ae9470a2ea97: Handover, with any minor outstanding items listed and agreed in writing.
487d5c1608afd0cd: Systems checklist: test before you look
0e59f73e0af88505: Flood test wet areas and roof terraces where the contract allows, or ask for records of tests carried out before tiling.
c4af28afac3bf39d: Check roof falls: water should run to outlets, not sit in puddles after washing down.
3c763d294298029a: Look for staining on ceilings below bathrooms, terraces and planters.
5b65e9ff79e0dda2: Check upstands and terminations at door thresholds to terraces. This is where water most often gets in.
6d9fded72aba179b: Inspect planter boxes and green roofs for drainage and root barriers.
1637169a0be708da: Run every indoor unit at once, on cooling, for several hours. Check each room reaches and holds its set temperature.
b03f230656264ef5: Ask for the commissioning records: airflow, refrigerant pressures, chilled water flow where relevant.
02d5289075888c95: Check condensate drains on every unit. Blocked or badly falling condensate lines are a common cause of ceiling leaks months later.
967b4d4b03628a9d: Listen for noise and vibration from outdoor units, especially near bedrooms and neighbours.
fb5669944147a7fa: Check fresh air and extract fans in bathrooms and kitchens actually move air, and that ducts terminate outside, not into a ceiling void.
950750748df143e8: Confirm access panels exist for every fan coil unit and valve.
16d675b38cb295aa: Test every socket, switch and light circuit. Label check: does the distribution board schedule match reality?
b8ba8fcd5cd53396: Check external lighting, timers and sensors.
2799258ac854bbc0: Test data points, Wi-Fi coverage, CCTV, intercom, gate and garage door controls.
8c386c35e8869bb2: If there is home automation, have the integrator demonstrate every scene and hand over admin access and passwords.
d8060e9c322118b0: Run every tap hot and cold. Check hot water reaches temperature in reasonable time at the furthest outlet.
cec7d4e9bf067f09: Fill every bath and basin to overflow level and let it drain. Watch for slow drainage and gurgling.
c34ca68c23c7f021: Lift manhole and gully covers; check they are clean, benched and free of construction debris.
7cb67f488a040bb5: Check water pressure across floors, and test the booster pump and water tank.
78a25595d0791057: Look for leaks under every sink and vanity, and at the water heater.
a0f966e48aa4aaf3: Leave filtration running for at least a day before inspection. Check water clarity and level stability: a falling level suggests a leak.
81e1780cfe72223b: Inspect tiles, copings and expansion joints.
c48d277b7910be99: Test lights, heater or chiller, cover, and any water features.
353484042391edec: Check the plant room: labelling, valves, access, ventilation and drainage.
3b698a7041fba028: Ask for the pool's pressure test records and the equipment warranties.
607f229e9ea573ed: Open, close and lock every window and sliding door. Large sliding panels should run smoothly without force.
c3d7e045df723dec: Check seals and gaskets for gaps, and look for daylight around frames.
c9f8d912dd498f5f: Inspect glass for scratches, chips and any marks indicating the wrong specification.
3e9817c40f4f09cd: Check external cladding, render and stone for cracks, staining, open joints and colour variation.
5a1dbded0dabfa25: After rain or a hose test, check inside for water at sills and corners.
101527585bdda266: Confirm shading devices and motorised blinds work.
5bb94b376d4cfdff: Check paving falls away from the house.
d40f17dd78058b7b: Inspect boundary walls, gates and joints.
8a23e1789de5deea: Run irrigation zones and check for leaks and coverage.
2019dd5243d30f6e: Look at landscaping drainage: water from the garden should not run towards thresholds.
07a36b1e661c2036: Inspect in daylight and again with artificial light at a low angle, which shows up uneven plaster and paint.
367f4c2a9bb0963b: Lippage between tiles, hollow tiles (tap them), grout consistency, stone sealing, chips, scratches on timber, gaps at skirtings
f3feab3d892c9d40: Cracks, uneven plaster, paint coverage and runs, straight shadow gaps and cornices, clean junctions with joinery
9169ed06859c9603: Swing, closing, gaps, ironmongery fixed and working, door stops fitted, no binding
49c44ca67ef352e2: Alignment, soft-close, internal finishes, edge banding, fixings into walls
fa38dd7d8f483a11: Appliances installed and tested, worktop joints, sealant, extract ducting, under-cabinet lighting
4919b1eb9be8253c: Silicone joints, shower screen seals, tile falls to drains, mirror and accessory fixing, no hollow tiles in wet areas
877bd6f910fe1092: Fixings solid, glass secure, handrails continuous, finishes undamaged
b966c41e0a5bf4ef: Damp patches, sump pumps tested, ventilation, waterproofing at construction joints
6747e2cd0d532f9d: Photograph each item, give it a number and location, and describe the remedy expected. "Paint poor in bedroom" will get a dab of paint. "Bedroom 2, north wall, paint coverage patchy across full wall, repaint wall to match" gets the wall repainted.
28eb44fa583fa1d1: What documents should you collect at handover?
b9ef347951114b90: Do not accept the keys without these, or at least a dated list of what is outstanding and when it will be delivered.
e0b81e980da3e3bf: Completion certificate from the relevant authority (Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits), plus any master developer completion or no-objection letters.
c0c6a1aaf53872e0: As-built drawings for architecture, structure and all MEP services, showing what was actually built, including concealed pipe and cable routes.
e627c123c2956665: Warranties and guarantees: waterproofing, AC equipment, pool, glazing and façade systems, roofing, appliances, pumps, and any structural guarantees. Check whose name they are in and when they start.
1991806db3973092: Operation and maintenance (O&M) manuals for every system, with maintenance schedules and supplier contacts.
02a63e4fc6452eb5: Test and commissioning certificates: electrical, plumbing pressure tests, AC commissioning, fire and life safety where applicable.
1e0e75a8e7d42ff2: Utility account details and confirmation of connections.
514a87c1fe971be1: Keys, access cards, remotes and passwords, with a signed schedule.
b8b9b99d62ddc089: Spare materials: tiles, stone and paint from the same batch, for future repairs.
b2fdcaa0444e4605: Under UAE law, the main contractor and the engineer carry a ten-year liability for serious structural defects from handover, now set out in Articles 821 to 824 of the new Civil Code (Charles Russell Speechlys). That covers structural matters, not leaking showers. The handover documents are what let you enforce the rest. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on how liability applies to your project.
9759d62759aea205: Most villa contracts include a defects liability period after handover, during which the contractor must come back and fix defects that appear. The length and the mechanics are set by your contract, so read it before handover, not after.
5186726f9f6302f1: Retention is money held back from payments and released in stages, often part at handover and the rest at the end of the defects period. Together with the final payment, it is your main leverage. Our general rule of thumb: do not release more than the contract requires until the agreed snags are closed and the handover documents are delivered. Check your contract and take legal advice before withholding sums the contractor considers due.
20a37e0a13ddd57a: How snag lists get closed out, and how they stall
e2cef83c5a60f80c: We spent two decades on the contractor's side of handovers. Here is what we know about how they go.
fe87a0079a3caa26: A clean, numbered list. A contractor's site manager can allocate a numbered list to trades in an hour. A vague list becomes an argument.
6da456bfbdd16e23: One list, one owner. When the owner, the family, the interior designer and the consultant all send separate lists, items get duplicated, contradicted and lost.
bc4ac1278945ac17: Money still on the table. On the contractor's side, the jobs we closed out fastest were the ones where a meaningful sum was still to be paid on completion.
9417eec2be92a028: Joint walkrounds. Walking the list together, item by item, and signing off what is closed stops the same items being reopened.
face78755c488ad1: Early release of money. Once the final payment and retention have gone, the snag list competes with every other job for the contractor's attention. It usually loses.
1ff2def5aa55e839: Trades demobilised. Subcontractors leave site once their package is paid. Getting a tiler back for three tiles is hard for the main contractor too.
226b6a7c659e08b1: Snags mixed with changes. If the list includes things you have changed your mind about, the contractor will treat the whole list as a variation request. Separate defects from new requests.
f19fc567df69af53: Moving in too early. Once furniture and family are in, it becomes difficult to prove who caused a scratch or a chip. Inspect and record before occupation.
27740973c294f1bf: No deadline. Agree a date for closing items, in writing, as part of handover.
b7bb48a09888dde6: We act for the owner at the end of the build, working alongside your registered consultant and contractor. We carry out independent client-side inspections, prepare a clear, numbered snag list, track the close-out, check the handover documents against what the contract requires, and advise on how retention and final payments should be handled commercially. Our snagging and handover service sets out how we work. If your villa is nearing completion, contact us.
95e8376023e6bac5: When should I snag a new villa in Dubai?
bf6c2c91a033826a: Inspect once the contractor says the work is complete and before you accept handover or release further payment. Ideally do a pre-handover inspection, let the contractor close items, then re-inspect. Published guidance allows around one to two months for snagging.
8bbfde4fd2b375e6: What is the defects liability period on a Dubai villa?
20626130739910de: It is whatever your contract says. Many contracts set a period, often a year, during which the contractor must return to fix defects. Check your contract and take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer if the wording is unclear.
7b13f7cf37c2b5a0: Should I pay the final instalment before the snags are fixed?
15a3a82f82ced0d2: In our experience, no. Hold the final payment and any retention in line with your contract until agreed snags are closed and the handover documents are delivered. Check what the contract allows before withholding anything.
ffb4e7e36f62ffca: Do I need a professional to snag my villa?
ab7e5cac73f9331b: You can do a first pass yourself with this checklist, but system testing, moisture readings and thermal checks benefit from experienced eyes and the right equipment.

f837b8dca6e4d42e: Contracts · 29 October 2026 · 8 min read · By Philip Chapman
2d8822c37927d6b2: A contractor's bid is a commercial strategy, not just a cost estimate: the margin is often planned in the gaps, not in the headline.
eda414d5f28adfcf: Provisional sums, preliminaries and variation rates are where an apparently cheap bid becomes an expensive project.
1453736787336b16: Programme float belongs to whoever the contract says it belongs to, and that decides who pays for delay.
154e3b008778edd7: A monthly valuation should be read line by line against work actually installed, not approved as a total.
2362e909ef56de7a: Your leverage peaks before handover and falls sharply once you have the keys and the retention is released.
cd6880375bc074de: How does a contractor actually price a villa bid?
7ffb0ce4fa6715cc: What are provisional sums, and why do they matter so much?
2188de321cb66dca: Why are preliminaries the line to watch?
5cc3b3b8f7a132e2: Why is the cheapest bid rarely the cheapest outcome?
410f5c5188c33b62: How should you read a monthly valuation?
75d125cae4d73f67: A builder knows that the price you sign is a starting point, that the margin on a job is often planned in the gaps rather than the headline, and that most owners never read the documents where those gaps sit. Provisional sums, preliminaries, variation rates, programme float and the monthly valuation are where a villa's real cost is decided. We spent 21 years on the contractor's side of premium residential building in the UK, and this is what we would want any owner to know before signing.
ea20ace8a35b4d6f: Nothing here is a criticism of contractors. Building is a hard, risky business with thin margins, and a good contractor is worth paying properly. But the commercial logic of the contractor's side is not the owner's logic, and the owner who understands it gets a better building for less trouble.
1accb36cbead3cb9: How does a contractor actually price a villa bid?
b604cbc7b4b3f359: Owners imagine a contractor adds up materials and labour, puts a margin on top, and sends the number. That is the estimate. The bid is something else.
b09a76d7373cd7f0: On the contractor's side, the first thing any builder prices is not the building. It is the risk in the documents. How complete was the design? Which items were vague? What was missing from the drawings that would obviously have to be built? Where would the client inevitably change their mind? Those answers decide how a contractor bids.
371decc595d9eb32: When the design is complete and the competition strong, contractors price tight, because there is little to recover later. When the design is loose, the market can afford to bid lower, because everyone knows the job will grow. That is the uncomfortable truth: an incomplete design does not just add risk, it invites a lower bid, which looks like good news to the owner and is often the opposite.
a02e137d787cf174: Contractors also price the client. A first-time owner who lives overseas, with no independent adviser, is a different commercial proposition from an experienced developer with a quantity surveyor checking every valuation. Nobody writes that on the bid, but it is in the number.
e834f43a7300ce53: Then there is the subcontract market. Much of a villa is built by specialist subcontractors: MEP, glazing, joinery, stone, pools. The main contractor's bid depends on quotes from them, and those quotes can be sharpened after the main contract is signed. Savings found after signature are the contractor's to keep unless the contract says otherwise.
a3c946e1b25bd102: Quay House, St Mawes, Cornwall. Built by P Chapman Construction.
cfc12f4d15906d27: What are provisional sums, and why do they matter so much?
c1cfc04cd3034bf3: A provisional sum is an allowance for something not yet designed or chosen. "Kitchen: AED X." "Lighting control: AED Y." When the actual item is selected, the contract sum moves to the real cost.
9d0299fb06eb7b5a: From the builder's side, provisional sums do three useful things for the contractor:
56f6c0b4b0204f50: They make the bid look lower. If the owner's documents leave the allowance to the contractor, a low allowance makes the total more competitive, and the real cost arrives later.
a620eedcd76ec7de: They move risk to the owner. Whatever the item eventually costs, the owner pays it.
aad16285582c7e15: They often carry their own mark-up and attendance. Read how the contract adjusts provisional sums: is the contractor's overhead and profit added to the difference, and is there extra time?
6a5c6cbf0cbd6c98: In Dubai, this is particularly relevant on luxury villas, where kitchens, wardrobes, lighting, automation, AV and loose specialist items are often left as allowances because the owner has not chosen yet. In our experience, a bid where these make up a large share of the total is not really a fixed price at all.
c0cc2c2733cf23fd: What to do: resolve as many items as you can before pricing. Where you cannot, set the provisional sums yourself, at realistic levels, so every bidder carries the same figure. Then compare bids on what is left.
e1193dc8e56e25a4: Why are preliminaries the line to watch?
0c50770a21dbfb09: Preliminaries are the cost of running the site: the site manager, welfare, security, temporary power and water, scaffolding, hoarding, plant, insurances, waste and so on. Turner & Townsend put contractor preliminaries in Dubai at 12–14% (as cited by PRASOON).
6b1fcaff67d0e8b1: The important point is that many preliminaries are time-related. They are priced per week or per month. That means:
4c022a6f1173b0a0: A contractor who prices a short programme can show a low preliminaries figure. If the programme then slips, the time-related costs reappear in an extension-of-time claim.
955d5a8249272ef9: Every week of delay that the contract attributes to the owner, through late decisions, late information or changes, carries a weekly cost.
3138e47bf0bbce3a: When we compared our own bids against competitors, an unusually low preliminaries figure usually meant one of two things: an unrealistic programme, or preliminary costs hidden elsewhere in the rates. Ask every bidder for a weekly breakdown of time-related preliminaries. It tells you what delay will cost before it happens.
adf3cd245d5b4c94: A variation is a change to the work. Some are genuine owner changes. Many are not; they arise because the drawings were unclear, two consultants' drawings disagreed, or something necessary was simply missing.
37c6e900787db739: On the contractor's side, the commercial team reads the contract documents looking for exactly these gaps, from the day the job is won. Every ambiguity is a potential variation. Every late answer to a request for information is a potential delay. This is ordinary practice, and a contractor who did not do it would not stay in business for long.
80e5cd6ecb57f28e: How a variation claim is typically assembled:
a8e2287beba62c10: The direct cost of the extra or changed work, priced at contract rates where they apply and at new rates where they do not. New rates are where the margin tends to be.
ff343252218ebe5a: Knock-on costs: work removed or redone, materials wasted, re-sequencing.
84301f53e336863e: Time: if the change affects the critical path, an extension of time, and with it time-related preliminaries.
27f577c61568ba7d: Disruption: loss of productivity from working out of sequence.
dc5fa31de6d57d3c: The defence is the same in every case: price the variation and agree its time effect before it is instructed, in writing. A variation agreed after the work is done is priced by one party, the one that did it. 5ec4074138842ccf: Float is the slack in a programme: the amount an activity can slip without delaying completion. Owners rarely think about it. Contractors think about it a great deal.
8c41b51aae280f74: If the contract is silent, the practical answer is usually that float is used by whoever needs it first. A contractor who has planned well keeps float in its own activities and presents a programme where the owner's decisions sit on the critical path, with no slack. Then any late owner decision, a tile not chosen, a sample not approved, causes immediate, claimable delay.
116c1d3fea041ec3: When reviewing a contractor's programme, look for:
9521fa44ffb67880: Owner decisions shown with no float, while the contractor's own activities have plenty.
086c7eadd94f5eb9: Durations for long-lead items that assume orders the owner has not yet been asked to approve.
ed424bfff8fa72d4: A programme without a clear list of information required from the owner, and when.
ac2d7990d4acb771: A decision schedule, agreed at the start, listing every owner choice and the latest date it can be made without delay, is one of the cheapest protections an owner can have.
470ff7ca4ae9436e: Why is the cheapest bid rarely the cheapest outcome?
790e78d56befab5c: Put the pieces together. The lowest bid often has some combination of low provisional sums, tight exclusions, a short programme with low preliminaries, and keen rates on the measured work but generous scope to recover through new rates. 5cbcf23dd2ec455a: None of that is visible in the total. 2455858710e80216: How should you read a monthly valuation?
e4c0226a49ba3603: Each month the contractor submits a valuation: the value of work done to date, less previous payments and retention. 6a3e83b6ec6d1869: Read a valuation line by line:
f23e508a7497ab97: Is the work actually installed? Not delivered, not "in progress", installed. Materials on site are a separate question, and paying for materials off site needs proof of ownership and insurance.
429e2d911acdc262: Do percentages match what you see? If the electrical installation is valued at 60%, is 60% of it actually done?
c99e6fb345c89b3a: Are variations valued only once agreed? Unagreed variations should be shown separately, not slipped into the total.

435aecdd46c817e4: The gap on many villa projects
e046357f411eace9: A private villa in Dubai brings together a master developer, a permitting authority, an architect, a registered consultant, a main contractor, specialist subcontractors and an interior designer. Each is competent. Each has their own commercial interest, and that is how it should be.
281967c62865bf7d: The result is a project in which each party covers its own part, but nobody is appointed to look at the whole from the owner's side: budget, programme, decisions and quality together. Owners fill the gap themselves, between their own work and family, often from another country. That is how good projects drift: a loose brief, a design that grows, a bid that looked cheapest, a payment made ahead of the work, a claim answered with opinion.
4acf9d3e634d3b0b: A client-side project manager closes the gap. We sit beside you, paid only by you, and work with everyone else to keep the project to what you agreed to pay for.
